uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns 1 when its result is strictly below the given threshold, otherwise 0. A result exactly equal to the threshold gives 0. This is the usual way to gate part of a larger formula on a condition, since multiplying by the result switches a term on or off.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The number the sub-formula's result is compared against. Written as a plain decimal value, not as a formula.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is tested. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns 1 when its result is strictly above the given threshold, otherwise 0. A result exactly equal to the threshold gives 0. Commonly used as a switch inside a larger formula, where multiplying by the result turns a term on or off.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The number the sub-formula's result is compared against. Written as a plain decimal value, not as a formula.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is tested. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns 1 when its result is exactly equal to the given value, otherwise 0. The comparison is on the raw fractional result, so it is only reliable for values that come out as whole numbers or exact halves.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The number the sub-formula's result must equal for the check to pass. Written as a plain decimal value, not as a formula.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is tested. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns 1 when its result differs from the given value, otherwise 0. This is the inverse of an exact-equality check, so any deviation at all, however small, counts as a match.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The number the sub-formula's result is compared against; the check passes when the result is anything else. Written as a plain decimal value, not as a formula.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is tested. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and clamps its result upward, returning whichever of the result and the given floor value is larger. Use it to stop a computed value from falling below a lower bound, for example keeping a damage figure from going negative.

arguments.name: floor
arguments.description: The lowest value the operand can produce. If the sub-formula's result is below this, this value is returned instead.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is clamped. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and clamps its result downward, returning whichever of the result and the given ceiling value is smaller. Use it to cap a computed value, for example limiting how much a stat can contribute to an effect.

arguments.name: ceiling
arguments.description: The highest value the operand can produce. If the sub-formula's result is above this, this value is returned instead.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is clamped. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns 1 when its result falls strictly between the two bounds, otherwise 0. Both ends are exclusive, so a result equal to either bound gives 0. The bounds may be given in either order; the operator works out which is the lower one, so the range is the same whichever way round they are written.

arguments.name: firstBound
arguments.description: One end of the allowed range, exclusive. It may be either the lower or the upper end.

arguments.name: secondBound
arguments.description: The other end of the allowed range, exclusive. It may be either the lower or the upper end.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is tested against the range. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns its magnitude, discarding the sign. A negative result becomes positive and a positive result is left alone, which is handy for turning a difference between two stats into a distance regardless of which is larger.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result has its sign stripped. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and rounds its result down to the nearest whole number. Rounding is always toward the lower value, so negative results move further from zero.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is rounded down. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and rounds its result up to the nearest whole number. Rounding is always toward the higher value, so negative results move closer to zero.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is rounded up. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and rounds its result to the nearest whole number. A result sitting exactly halfway between two whole numbers settles on the even one, so 2.5 becomes 2 and 3.5 becomes 4.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is rounded to the nearest whole number. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula and returns 1 when its result is zero or negative, otherwise 0. This inverts a condition, so wrapping a check in it makes a term apply exactly when the check fails.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula whose result is inverted. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula, passes its result straight through unchanged, and also posts the sub-formula's text and its computed value to the on-screen debug readout for about ten seconds. Wrap a piece of a formula in it while tuning to watch what that piece actually produces during play; it has no effect on the result itself.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula to evaluate, display and return. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula as though a specific map tile were the tile being targeted, and returns its result. Anything inside the sub-formula that asks about the targeted tile sees the coordinates given here instead of the real one, which lets a formula probe a fixed spot on the map. The caster and target actors are left untouched.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column of the map tile that the sub-formula should treat as the targeted tile.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row of the map tile that the sub-formula should treat as the targeted tile.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula evaluated against the substituted tile. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula with the caster and the target exchanged, and returns its result. Inside it, everything that reads the caster reads the original target and the other way round, which lets one formula be written once and applied in both directions.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula evaluated with the two actors exchanged. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula as though a named actor were the caster, and returns its result. The named actor is looked up among the actors currently in the zone and in the fleets, and the name may also be a global variable holding an actor's ID. If no such actor is present the sub-formula runs with no caster at all, which usually makes caster-based terms come out as zero.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world to stand in as the caster. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula evaluated with the substituted caster. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Evaluates the trailing sub-formula as though a named actor were the target, and returns its result. The named actor is looked up among the actors currently in the zone and in the fleets, and the name may also be a global variable holding an actor's ID. If no such actor is present the sub-formula runs with no target at all, which usually makes target-based terms come out as zero.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world to stand in as the target. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

arguments.name: formula
arguments.description: The sub-formula evaluated with the substituted target. It swallows everything to the end of the operand, so it may itself be several colon-separated pieces.

uses.description: Reads one of the caster's actor values, including every buff, debuff and equipment bonus currently applied to it. Writing rank instead of an actor value name gives the rank of the action or ability the formula belongs to. If the name matches no actor value the caster's own named properties are searched as a fallback, with numbers passed through and a true flag coming out as 1. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to read. The special name rank yields the action or ability rank instead, and a name that is not an actor value is looked up as one of the caster's own properties.

uses.description: Reads the caster's base value for an actor value, before any buffs, debuffs or equipment bonuses are counted. Writing rank instead of an actor value name gives the rank of the action or ability the formula belongs to. With no caster the operand is 0, and an actor value the caster does not have comes out as -1.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to read the unmodified base of. The special name rank yields the action or ability rank instead.

uses.description: Reads one of the target's actor values, including every buff, debuff and equipment bonus currently applied to it. If the name matches no actor value the target's own named properties are searched as a fallback, with numbers passed through and a true flag coming out as 1. With no target the operand is 0. Unlike the caster reader, this one has no special handling for rank.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to read. A name that is not an actor value is looked up as one of the target's own properties instead.

uses.description: Reads the target's base value for an actor value, before any buffs, debuffs or equipment bonuses are counted. Writing rank instead of an actor value name gives the rank of the action or ability the formula belongs to. With no target the operand is 0, and an actor value the target does not have comes out as -1.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to read the unmodified base of. The special name rank yields the action or ability rank instead.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the caster's actor values currently sits at exactly 1, otherwise 0. This is the usual shorthand for testing an on/off status that is applied as an actor value. With no caster the operand is 0, and naming an actor value that does not exist reports an error.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to test for the value 1. Buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses are included in the value tested.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the caster's actor values is exactly equal to a given number, otherwise 0. The value tested includes every buff, debuff and equipment bonus in effect. With no caster the operand is 0, and naming an actor value that does not exist reports an error.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to test.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The number the actor value must match exactly for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the target's actor values is exactly equal to a given number, otherwise 0. The value tested includes every buff, debuff and equipment bonus in effect. With no target the operand is 0, and naming an actor value that does not exist reports an error.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to test.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The number the actor value must match exactly for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the caster's actor values is strictly above a given number, otherwise 0. A value exactly equal to the number gives 0. The value tested includes every buff, debuff and equipment bonus in effect, and with no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to test.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The number the actor value must exceed for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the target's actor values is strictly above a given number, otherwise 0. A value exactly equal to the number gives 0. The value tested includes every buff, debuff and equipment bonus in effect, and with no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to test.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The number the actor value must exceed for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the caster's actor values is strictly below a given number, otherwise 0. A value exactly equal to the number gives 0. The value tested includes every buff, debuff and equipment bonus in effect, and with no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to test.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The number the actor value must fall below for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the target's actor values is strictly below a given number, otherwise 0. A value exactly equal to the number gives 0. The value tested includes every buff, debuff and equipment bonus in effect, and with no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to test.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The number the actor value must fall below for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the target's actor values currently sits at exactly 1, otherwise 0. This is the usual shorthand for testing an on/off status that is applied as an actor value. With no target the operand is 0, and naming an actor value that does not exist reports an error.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to test for the value 1. Buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses are included in the value tested.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the target's actor values currently sits at exactly 99, otherwise 0. Ninety-nine is the level the game's meter-style actor values reach when they are full, so this tests for a maxed-out meter. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to test for the value 99. Buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses are included in the value tested.

uses.description: Reads the same actor value from both the caster and the target and yields the larger of the two. Both readings include buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses. If either actor is missing the operand is 0, so it only produces a figure when both sides of the exchange are present.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from both the caster and the target; the higher of the two readings is returned.

uses.description: Reports how long the caster's longest-running effect on a given actor value still has to run. When several effects touch the same actor value the largest remaining duration wins. Effects that never tick down report their marker value instead of a countdown: -1 for an effect with no time limit and -2 for one that permanently altered the base value. If nothing at all is affecting that actor value the operand is -999, so test for a positive result rather than for non-zero.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to look for timed effects on.

uses.description: Reports how long the target's longest-running effect on a given actor value still has to run. When several effects touch the same actor value the largest remaining duration wins. Effects that never tick down report their marker value instead of a countdown: -1 for an effect with no time limit and -2 for one that permanently altered the base value. If nothing at all is affecting that actor value the operand is -999, so test for a positive result rather than for non-zero.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to look for timed effects on.

uses.description: Adds up only the contributions that one particular source is making to one of the caster's actor values, ignoring the base value and every other contributor. Use it to ask how much of a stat a specific buff, item or ability is responsible for. If the caster has no such actor value the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to measure.

arguments.name: sourceID
arguments.description: The ID of the effect definition that applied the contributions to count. Only effects recorded as coming from this source are added up.

uses.description: Adds up only the contributions that one particular source is making to one of the target's actor values, ignoring the base value and every other contributor. Use it to ask how much of a stat a specific buff, item or ability is responsible for. If the target has no such actor value the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to measure.

arguments.name: sourceID
arguments.description: The ID of the effect definition that applied the contributions to count. Only effects recorded as coming from this source are added up.

uses.description: Reads one of the caster's actor values as it would stand if one particular source were not contributing to it. The base value and every other buff and penalty are counted as normal; only the named source is left out. An actor value the game does not define comes out as -1.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to read.

arguments.name: sourceID
arguments.description: The ID of the effect definition whose contributions are excluded from the total.

uses.description: Reads one of the target's actor values as it would stand if one particular source were not contributing to it. The base value and every other buff and penalty are counted as normal; only the named source is left out. An actor value the game does not define comes out as -1.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to read.

arguments.name: sourceID
arguments.description: The ID of the effect definition whose contributions are excluded from the total.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster is currently under a temporary penalty to a given actor value, otherwise 0. It looks for an effect on that actor value whose contribution works out as zero or worse and which is still on a countdown; permanent adjustments and effects that have run out do not count. Use it to tell an actively-applied debuff apart from a naturally low stat.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the caster's actor values to check for an active penalty.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is currently under a temporary penalty to a given actor value, otherwise 0. It looks for an effect on that actor value whose contribution works out as zero or worse and which is still on a countdown; permanent adjustments and effects that have run out do not count. Use it to tell an actively-applied debuff apart from a naturally low stat.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which of the target's actor values to check for an active penalty.

uses.description: Reads a named property of the weapon the caster is currently swinging. Recognised names are power for the weapon's damage power, maxRange for the reach of its attack including any range bonus, weight, throwDamageMod and throwRangePenalty for its throwing characteristics, and magnitude, duration or chance for the corresponding figure on the weapon's own attack. Giving an element name instead asks whether the weapon satisfies that element's requirements, returning 1 when it does. Anything else, or a caster with no weapon in that hand, yields 0.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.description: Which weapon property to read: power, maxRange, weight, throwDamageMod, throwRangePenalty, magnitude, duration, chance, or the name of an element to test the weapon's element requirements against.

uses.description: Reads a named property of the caster's other weapon, the one not being used for the attack this formula belongs to. It accepts the same property names as the main-hand reader: power, maxRange, weight, throwDamageMod, throwRangePenalty, magnitude, duration, chance, or an element name to test that hand's element requirements. Use it for dual-wielding rules that need to look at the opposite hand. Anything else, or a caster with no weapon in that hand, yields 0.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.description: Which property of the opposite-hand weapon to read: power, maxRange, weight, throwDamageMod, throwRangePenalty, magnitude, duration, chance, or the name of an element to test that weapon's element requirements against.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster has a given actor class in any of its four class slots, otherwise 0. Empty slots never match, so an actor with no classes at all always gives 0. Use it to make an action or bonus apply only to characters of a particular profession.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class to look for in the caster's primary, secondary, third and fourth class slots.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target belongs to a named combat team, otherwise 0. Combat teams are the groupings the battle uses to decide who fights alongside whom, so this distinguishes sides in a multi-way fight. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: combatTeam
arguments.description: Name of the combat team the target must be on, matched exactly.

uses.description: Gives the map column that a named actor is currently standing on. The actor is looked up among those present in the zone and in the fleets, and the name may also be a global variable holding an actor's ID. If no such actor is around the operand is 0, which is also a real map column, so pair it with a separate existence check when that matters.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world whose column is wanted. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Gives the map row that a named actor is currently standing on. The actor is looked up among those present in the zone and in the fleets, and the name may also be a global variable holding an actor's ID. If no such actor is around the operand is 0, which is also a real map row, so pair it with a separate existence check when that matters.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world whose row is wanted. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Gives the distance in tiles between two named actors, measured the way the game measures movement and reach rather than as a straight line. Both actors are looked up among those present in the zone and in the fleets. If either one is missing the operand is 0.

arguments.name: firstActorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor at one end of the measurement. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

arguments.name: secondActorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor at the other end of the measurement. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Counts the queued actions that are aimed at the tile this formula is being evaluated against, so a formula can react to how much incoming fire a spot is already going to take. Naming an action narrows the count to queued copies of that action and also adds any of it that are waiting in the execution queue; leaving the name out counts every queued action aimed at the tile. A name that is not a real action falls back to counting everything, so a typo silently widens the count. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: Restricts the count to queued copies of this action, and adds in any copies of it already waiting to execute. Leave it out to count every queued action aimed at the tile.

uses.description: Counts the queued actions aimed at the tile this formula is being evaluated against, and on top of that the pending tile effects sitting on that same tile. Naming an ID narrows the action count to that action, adds any copies of it already waiting to execute, and adds pending tile effects whose own ID matches. Leaving the name out counts every queued action aimed at the tile and no tile effects at all. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: Restricts the action count to this action and adds in any copies already waiting to execute; the same text is also matched against the IDs of pending tile effects on the tile. Leave it out to count every queued action aimed at the tile and skip tile effects entirely.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies that fall inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the target's tile. Incapacitated actors are skipped, and allegiance is judged by whether an actor is hostile in the same sense as the caster, so the caster itself is included when it stands in the shape. If either the caster or the target is missing the operand is 0.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the target's tile when deciding which tiles to search.

uses.description: Counts how many of the player's party members are standing within a given distance of a fixed map position. Distance is measured in tiles the way the game measures movement and reach. It looks at the whole party, not only the actors in the current scene.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column of the map position to measure from.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row of the map position to measure from.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles away a party member may be and still count. Leave it out for a radius of 2.

uses.description: Looks at every actor standing inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the caster's tile and oriented to the way the caster is facing, and counts them. Adding an actor value name makes it add up that actor value across those actors instead of counting heads, which is how you total the health or the armour of everyone caught in a blast. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the caster's tile; it is rotated to match the caster's facing.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: When given, this actor value is read from each actor found and the readings are summed. Leave it out to count the actors instead.

uses.description: Looks at every actor standing inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the target's tile and counts them. When there is no target the shape is laid over the tile being targeted instead, so it still works for an action aimed at empty ground. Adding an actor value name makes it add up that actor value across those actors instead of counting heads. Unlike the caster-centred version the shape is not rotated to any facing.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the target's tile, or over the targeted tile when there is no target actor.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: When given, this actor value is read from each actor found and the readings are summed. Leave it out to count the actors instead.

uses.description: Returns 1 while the player is in conversation with a named actor, otherwise 0. Use it in dialog requirements to make an option or a line appear only when a particular character is the one being spoken to.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor the player must currently be talking to, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is currently allowed to take an action, otherwise 0. As well as the usual turn-order and interface rules this accounts for the zone itself forbidding action, and for items on the actor's own tile that suppress acting, including ones that only do so in peaceful zones. An actor that is not present in the world gives 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world whose ability to act is being tested. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is currently allowed to move, otherwise 0. This follows the game's ordinary rules about whose turn it is and whether the interface is accepting movement. An actor that is not present in the world gives 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world whose ability to move is being tested. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Reports whether a named actor is currently allowed to move: 1 when it is, 0 when it is not. Despite the name it runs the same movement check as the ordinary movement test rather than a separate item-handling check, so it will not tell you about restrictions that apply only to picking things up. An actor that is not present in the world gives 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor in the world being tested. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item the target is carrying, looking inside containers in its inventory as well as the top level. When there is no target actor it counts that item lying on the tile being targeted instead. With neither a target nor a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count. Quantities are added up, so a stack of five counts as five.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item are lying on the ground within a number of tiles of the target, adding up stack quantities. When there is no target actor the search is centred on the tile being targeted instead. With neither a target nor a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to look for on the ground.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the centre to search.

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the ground within a number of tiles of the target that carry a given special property, adding up stack quantities. When there is no target actor the search is centred on the tile being targeted instead. Use it for rules that care about a kind of item rather than one particular item, such as anything flammable nearby.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the centre to search.

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the ground within a number of tiles of the target that give off light, adding up stack quantities. The search ignores walls and line of sight, so it reaches items behind cover. When there is no target actor the search is centred on the tile being targeted instead.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the centre to search.

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the ground within a number of tiles of the target that belong to a given item category, adding up stack quantities. The search ignores walls and line of sight, so it reaches items behind cover. When there is no target actor the search is centred on the tile being targeted instead.

arguments.name: itemCategory
arguments.description: The item category to look for; only items of this category are counted.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the centre to search.

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the ground inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the caster's tile, but only those whose named item property matches a given value. Stack quantities are added up. The comparison is made on the property's text form with punctuation and letter case smoothed out, so a value like Weapon matches weapon. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the caster's tile. It is not rotated to the caster's facing.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the item property to test, written exactly as it appears on an item definition. A name that is not a real item property makes the count come out as 0.

arguments.name: propertyValue
arguments.description: The value that property must have for an item to be counted.

uses.description: Counts every item lying on the ground inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the caster's tile, adding up stack quantities. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the caster's tile. It is not rotated to the caster's facing.

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the ground inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the target's tile, but only those whose named item property matches a given value. Stack quantities are added up. When there is no target actor the shape is laid over the tile being targeted instead. The comparison is made on the property's text form with punctuation and letter case smoothed out, so a value like Weapon matches weapon.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the target's tile, or over the targeted tile when there is no target actor.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the item property to test, written exactly as it appears on an item definition. A name that is not a real item property makes the count come out as 0.

arguments.name: propertyValue
arguments.description: The value that property must have for an item to be counted.

uses.description: Counts every item lying on the ground inside a named area-of-effect shape laid over the target's tile, adding up stack quantities. When there is no target actor the shape is laid over the tile being targeted instead.

arguments.name: aoeID
arguments.description: The area-of-effect shape to lay over the target's tile, or over the targeted tile when there is no target actor.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is carrying strictly more than a given number of an item, otherwise 0. Containers in the target's inventory are searched as well as the top level, and stack quantities are added up. When there is no target actor the items lying on the tile being targeted are counted instead.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The count must exceed this number for the check to pass; an exact match gives 0.

uses.description: Returns 1 when more than a given number of an item exist anywhere in the current zone, otherwise 0. Everything in the zone is counted, on the ground and in inventories alike, so this is a way to ask whether a resource is still plentiful. An exact match on the number gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count across the zone.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The zone-wide count must exceed this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item are lying on one specific map tile, named by its coordinates. Stack quantities are added up, so a pile of five counts as five. The tile is given outright, so this works regardless of what the formula is being aimed at.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column of the tile to look at.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row of the tile to look at.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count on that tile.

uses.description: Returns 1 when at least one of a given item is lying on the tile this formula is being evaluated against, otherwise 0. This form reports presence rather than a count, however large the pile. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to look for on the targeted tile.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item exist anywhere in the current zone, on the ground and in inventories alike. Stack quantities are added up. Use it for rules about how much of a resource the whole area still holds.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count across the zone.

uses.description: Counts how many items carrying a given special property exist anywhere in the current zone, on the ground and in inventories alike. Use it for rules about a kind of item rather than one particular item, such as how much flammable material is left in the area.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

uses.description: Adds together how many of a given item exist in the current zone and how many the player's people are carrying, so an item that is both lying about and in a pack is counted twice over. The party side of the sum covers party members, the rest of the player's crew, the stash and anything held by the cursor.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count in the zone and across the player's people.

uses.description: Counts the items carrying a given special property that the target is holding, searching containers in its inventory as well as the top level. When there is no target actor it counts items with that property lying on the tile being targeted instead, ignoring any that are buried. With neither a target nor a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

uses.description: Counts the items carrying a given special property that are lying on the tile this formula is being evaluated against, ignoring any that are buried. It always looks at the ground, never inside a target's pack, so it reports what is underfoot at the aimed-at spot. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

uses.description: Counts the items lying on the tile this formula is being evaluated against whose element reactions fire a given action, adding up stack quantities. An item with several reactions to that same action is counted once per reaction. Use it to ask whether the ground at a spot will explode, catch light or otherwise respond in a particular way. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action an item's element reaction must fire for that item to be counted.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item are lying on the ground under the target, adding up stack quantities. This looks at the tile the target is standing on, not at what the target is carrying. When there is no target actor it counts on the tile being targeted instead, and with neither the operand is 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count on the ground under the target.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item are lying on the ground under the caster, adding up stack quantities. This looks at the tile the caster is standing on, not at what the caster is carrying. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count on the ground under the caster.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a fresh copy of a given item could be dropped onto the tile this formula is being evaluated against, otherwise 0. It accounts for whatever already occupies the tile, so it is the check to make before an effect tries to place something on the ground.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose placement is being tested; a new one is made up for the test rather than taken from anyone's pack.

uses.description: Gives the base worth of an item as written on its definition, before any port or merchant adjustment. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose base worth is wanted.

uses.description: Gives the base worth recorded on an actor type, which for ships is the price the hull is reckoned at. An actor type name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type whose recorded worth is wanted.

uses.description: Gives what an item currently costs to buy, as opposed to the flat worth written on its definition. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose purchase price is wanted.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item the player's people have between them: the party members, the rest of the crew aboard the player's fleet, the stash, and anything currently held by the cursor. Containers are searched, but locked ones are skipped, and stack quantities are added up.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count across the player's people and storage.

uses.description: Counts how many items carrying a given special property the player's people have between them: the party members, the rest of the crew aboard the player's fleet, the stash, and anything currently held by the cursor. Containers are searched, including locked ones, and stack quantities are added up.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's people hold at least a given number of the item named by a global variable, otherwise 0. The count covers party members, the rest of the crew aboard the player's fleet, the stash and anything held by the cursor. Unlike most of the comparison operators this one passes on an exact match as well.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the ID of the item to count.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The count must reach this number for the check to pass; reaching it exactly still passes.

uses.description: Counts how many of the item named by a global variable the player's people hold, across the party members, the rest of the crew aboard the player's fleet, the stash and anything held by the cursor. Containers are searched but locked ones are skipped. Use it when the item in question is decided by the story rather than fixed in advance.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the ID of the item to count.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the ship's hold contains at least a given number of an item, otherwise 0. Containers stowed in the hold are searched as well. Reaching the number exactly still passes.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count in the hold.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The count must reach this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item are stowed in the ship's hold, searching containers in the hold as well and adding up stack quantities. This is the cargo the ship is carrying, not what anyone has in their personal pack.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count in the hold.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the ship's hold contains at least a given number of items carrying a special property, otherwise 0. Containers stowed in the hold are searched as well. Reaching the number exactly still passes.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The count must reach this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Counts how many items carrying a given special property are stowed in the ship's hold, searching containers in the hold as well and adding up stack quantities. Use it for rules about a kind of cargo rather than one particular item.

arguments.name: specialProperty
arguments.description: The item special property to look for; only items carrying it are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the ship's hold contains at least a given number of the item named by a global variable, otherwise 0. Containers stowed in the hold are searched as well, and reaching the number exactly still passes. Use it when the item in question is decided by the story rather than fixed in advance.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the ID of the item to count.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The count must reach this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Counts how many of the item named by a global variable are stowed in the ship's hold, searching containers in the hold as well and adding up stack quantities. Use it when the item in question is decided by the story rather than fixed in advance.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the ID of the item to count.

uses.description: Returns 1 when every entry on a given item's make-into list has a global variable of the same name standing at 1 or more, otherwise 0. Those variables are the game's record that each of those items has been placed in the world, so this asks whether a whole set has been spawned. An item with an empty make-into list always gives 1.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose make-into list names the entries to check. Each entry doubles as the name of the global variable that records it.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named item has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list, so this also answers questions like whether an item carries a particular special property. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose definition is inspected.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the weapon in the caster's favoured hand has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Only a real weapon counts: the held item must be of the weapon category and must have an attack of its own, so a shield or a tool gives 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the weapon in the caster's off hand has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Only a real weapon counts: the held item must be of the weapon category and must have an attack of its own, so a shield or a tool gives 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when whatever the caster has in a numbered equipment slot has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Unlike the weapon-hand checks this accepts any item at all, so it works for armour, tools and trinkets. An empty slot, a slot number out of range, or a first value that is not a whole number all give 0.

arguments.name: slot
arguments.description: Which of the caster's equipment slots to look at, counting from zero. The hands are the first slots.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property straight off a named item's definition and yields it as a number. Any property whose text form parses as a number can be read this way. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose definition is read.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property off the definition of the weapon in the caster's favoured hand. Only a real weapon counts: the held item must be of the weapon category and must have an attack of its own, so a shield or a tool gives 0. An empty hand also gives 0.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property off the definition of the weapon in the caster's off hand. Only a real weapon counts: the held item must be of the weapon category and must have an attack of its own, so a shield or a tool gives 0. An empty hand also gives 0.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property off the definition of whatever the caster has in a numbered equipment slot. Unlike the weapon-hand readers this accepts any item at all, so it works for armour, tools and trinkets. An empty slot, a slot number out of range, or a first value that is not a whole number all give 0.

arguments.name: slot
arguments.description: Which of the caster's equipment slots to look at, counting from zero. The hands are the first slots.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Returns 1 when any item currently picked up on the cursor has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. This is about what the player has literally lifted out of an inventory, not what anyone has equipped or stowed. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an item definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster is wearing or wielding something belonging to a named exclusive equipment category, otherwise 0. Only the five main equipment slots are examined: the two hands, which count only for weapons whose category is marked as applying to weapons, the armour slot, and the two accessory slots. Letter case and punctuation in the category name are smoothed out before comparing.

arguments.name: equipmentCategory
arguments.description: The exclusive equipment category to look for, as written on an item definition.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is wearing or wielding something belonging to a named exclusive equipment category, otherwise 0. Only the five main equipment slots are examined: the two hands, which count only for weapons whose category is marked as applying to weapons, the armour slot, and the two accessory slots. Letter case and punctuation in the category name are smoothed out before comparing.

arguments.name: equipmentCategory
arguments.description: The exclusive equipment category to look for, as written on an item definition.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is present in the world, otherwise 0. The lookup covers the actors in the current zone and in the fleets, and the name may also be a global variable holding an actor's ID. Use it to check that a character is around before asking anything else about it.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to look for. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is standing on one specific map tile, otherwise 0. Both the actor and the tile are named outright, so this does not depend on what the formula is aimed at. An actor that is not present in the world gives 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor whose position is being tested. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column the actor must be standing on.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row the actor must be standing on.

uses.description: Counts how many actors of a given actor type are in the current zone, including any that are queued to appear but have not been placed yet. Use it for rules that scale with how many of a creature are on the field, or to check that a spawn has happened.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type to count.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the actor this formula is aimed at is the one named, otherwise 0. Be careful with names the game does not know: when there is no target at all, an unrecognised name also gives 1, because both sides of the comparison come out as nothing.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor the target must be. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the actor this formula is aimed at is standing on one specific map tile, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0. Use it to make an effect apply only when the victim is on a particular spot.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column the target must be standing on.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row the target must be standing on.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target belongs to a named faction, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0. Use it for rules that treat the crews of different powers differently.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction the target must belong to, matched exactly.

uses.description: Adds up one actor value across every actor in the current zone, friend and foe alike. Each reading includes that actor's buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses. Use it for effects that scale with the whole field, such as total remaining health.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from each actor and summed.

uses.description: Adds up one actor value across every actor taking turns in the current battle. Each reading includes that actor's buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses. Outside of combat the operand is 0, so it is safe to use in formulas that also run on the world map.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from each combatant and summed.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster is of a given actor type, otherwise 0. With no caster the operand is 0. Use it to make a shared action behave differently in the hands of a particular creature.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type the caster must be, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is of a given actor type, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0. Use it for bonuses against a particular kind of creature.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type the target must be, matched exactly.

uses.description: Gives how many of a given actor type the player has killed over the whole game so far. The tally is kept in the save, so it carries across zones and voyages. An actor type nothing has been killed of gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type whose lifetime kill tally is wanted.

uses.description: Gives how many of the actor type named by a global variable the player has killed over the whole game so far. The tally is kept in the save, so it carries across zones and voyages. Use it when the creature in question is decided by the story rather than fixed in advance.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the actor type whose kill tally is wanted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster knows a given support ability, otherwise 0. With no caster the operand is 0. Use it to give an action a bonus that only applies to characters who have learned a particular passive.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability the caster must know, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster does not know a given support ability, otherwise 0. With no caster the operand is 0, so an absent caster reads the same as one who does know it. Use it for a penalty or a fallback that applies only to characters lacking a particular passive.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability the caster must not know, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target knows a given support ability, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0. Use it for effects that react to what the victim can do, such as an attack that works differently against someone who can parry.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability the target must know, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target does not know a given support ability, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0, so an absent target reads the same as one who does know it. Use it for effects that only land on someone lacking a particular defence.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability the target must not know, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor type has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list. An actor type name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type whose definition is inspected.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an actor type definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property straight off a named actor type's definition and yields it as a number. Any property whose text form parses as a number can be read this way. An actor type name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type whose definition is read.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an actor type definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor belongs to one of the fleets sailing the world, otherwise 0. This finds ships and crews that are travelling as part of a fleet rather than standing in the current scene.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to look for among the fleets.

uses.description: Gives the effective crew strength of a named ship: how many hands it has that are still on their feet. Crew who are down or drowning do not count at all, and badly wounded crew count as half a person, so the result can come out on a half. A ship that is not present in the world gives 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the ship whose effective crew strength is wanted. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Gives the plain head count of a named ship's crew, counting everyone aboard whatever state they are in. Unlike the effective-strength reading, the wounded and the unconscious each count as one. A ship that is not present in the world gives 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the ship whose crew is being counted. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Gives how many separate item stacks are stowed in a fleet's shared cargo hold. A stack of twenty planks counts as one, so this measures how full the hold is rather than how much is in it. A fleet that cannot be found gives 0.

arguments.name: fleetActorID
arguments.description: ID of any ship or commodore in the fleet; the fleet it belongs to is the one measured. The special names enemyFleet and assistFleet pick out the fleets fighting the current battle.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item are stowed in a fleet's shared cargo hold, adding up stack quantities. By default the fleet is the one the target belongs to, which is how you ask what the ship you are boarding is carrying. An item the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to count in the hold.

arguments.name: fleetActorID
arguments.description: ID of any ship or commodore in the fleet to search; the special names enemyFleet and assistFleet pick out the fleets fighting the current battle. Leave it out to search the fleet the target belongs to.

uses.description: Gives how many ships a fleet still has afloat, leaving out any that have been sunk or disabled. A fleet that cannot be found gives 0.

arguments.name: fleetActorID
arguments.description: ID of any ship or commodore in the fleet; the fleet it belongs to is the one counted. The special names enemyFleet and assistFleet pick out the fleets fighting the current battle.

uses.description: Gives how many ships a fleet has on its roster, counting sunk and disabled ones as well as those still afloat. A fleet that cannot be found gives 0.

arguments.name: fleetActorID
arguments.description: ID of any ship or commodore in the fleet; the fleet it belongs to is the one counted. The special names enemyFleet and assistFleet pick out the fleets fighting the current battle.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a fleet's roster includes at least one ship of a given actor type, otherwise 0. Sunk and disabled ships still count, since the whole roster is searched. By default the fleet is the one the target belongs to. An actor type the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The ship type to look for on the fleet's roster.

arguments.name: fleetActorID
arguments.description: ID of any ship or commodore in the fleet to search; the special names enemyFleet and assistFleet pick out the fleets fighting the current battle. Leave it out to search the fleet the target belongs to.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a fleet is marked as elite, otherwise 0. Elite fleets are the tougher, better-equipped ones the world spawns. A fleet that cannot be found gives 0.

arguments.name: fleetActorID
arguments.description: ID of any ship or commodore in the fleet; the fleet it belongs to is the one checked. The special names enemyFleet and assistFleet pick out the fleets fighting the current battle.

uses.description: Adds up one actor value across everyone crewing the caster's ship. It only produces a figure when the caster is itself a ship; for an ordinary character the operand is 0. Each reading includes that crew member's buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from each crew member and summed.

uses.description: Adds up one actor value across everyone crewing the target's ship. It only produces a figure when the target is itself a ship; for an ordinary character the operand is 0. Each reading includes that crew member's buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from each crew member and summed.

uses.description: Returns 1 when an actor class is one the player is allowed to pick, otherwise 0. Classes whose ID starts with dummy are always rejected, since those are placeholders rather than real professions.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class being tested.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a given actor value is one of the stats an actor class is built around, otherwise 0. These are the stats the class advances and displays, not everything a character of that class happens to have.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose stat list is searched.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The stat to look for on that class.

uses.description: Gives how many stats an actor class is built around. An actor class the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose stats are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a given action is on an actor class's list of learnable actions, otherwise 0. This asks what the class can teach, not what any particular character has learned.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose action list is searched.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action to look for on that class.

uses.description: Gives how many actions an actor class can teach. An actor class the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose actions are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a given support ability is on an actor class's list of learnable passives, otherwise 0. This asks what the class can teach, not what any particular character has learned.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose support ability list is searched.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability to look for on that class.

uses.description: Gives how many support abilities an actor class can teach. An actor class the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose support abilities are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has discovered an actor class and may train characters in it, otherwise 0. Classes whose ID starts with dummy are always rejected, since those are placeholders rather than real professions.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class being tested.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster meets whatever conditions an actor class sets on who may take it, otherwise 0. With no caster the operand is 0. Use it to gate an option on whether this particular character could train as that profession.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose entry conditions are checked against the caster.

uses.description: Counts how many of an actor class's actions the caster has bought at least one rank in. It measures progress through the class's action list rather than mastery of it. With no caster, or an actor class the game does not know, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose action list is checked against what the caster has bought.

uses.description: Counts how many of an actor class's support abilities the caster has bought at least one rank in. It measures progress through the class's passive list rather than mastery of it. With no caster, or an actor class the game does not know, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose support ability list is checked against what the caster has bought.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster has taken every action of an actor class all the way to its top rank, otherwise 0. A single action left short of its maximum brings the whole thing to 0. With no caster, or an actor class the game does not know, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose actions must all be at their top rank.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the caster has taken every support ability of an actor class all the way to its top rank, otherwise 0. A single ability left short of its maximum brings the whole thing to 0. With no caster, or an actor class the game does not know, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose support abilities must all be at their top rank.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is one of the player's party members, otherwise 0. The lookup only considers actors standing in the current zone, so a party member away with a fleet does not register.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to look for in the party. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when any of the player's party members is standing on one specific map tile, otherwise 0. The tile is named outright, so this does not depend on what the formula is aimed at.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column the party member must be standing on.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row the party member must be standing on.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is part of the landing party, the group that goes ashore when the player leaves the ship, otherwise 0. This is the recorded roster rather than who happens to be standing where.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to look for on the landing party roster, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named actor is either one of the player's party members or one of the crew aboard the player's fleet, otherwise 0. Use it for rules that should cover everyone sailing with the player, not just the away team.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to look for among the party and the crew. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's fleet has at least one ship of a given actor type still afloat, otherwise 0. Sunk and disabled ships are left out. With no player fleet at all the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The ship type to look for in the player's fleet.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the character the player is actually playing as occupies a given position in the party order, otherwise 0. Positions are counted from zero, and a position past the end of the party gives 0.

arguments.name: partySlot
arguments.description: Position in the party order to test, counting from zero.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the character the player is actually playing as is of a given actor type, otherwise 0. Use it for content that only applies to a particular player character.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type the main player character must be, matched exactly.

uses.description: Adds up one actor value across every member of the player's party, wherever they are. Each reading includes that member's buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses. Use it for effects that scale with the party as a whole, such as its total remaining health.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from each party member and summed.

uses.description: Adds up one actor value across the crew aboard the player's fleet, leaving out anyone who is also a party member so the two totals do not overlap. Each reading includes that crew member's buffs, debuffs and equipment bonuses. With no player fleet the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value read from each crew member and summed.

uses.description: Gives how many times the caster has used a given action. The tally is kept per character, so it answers how practised this particular fighter is with that move. With no caster, or an action the caster has never used, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action whose use tally is wanted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the actor currently picked up on the cursor has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. This is about a character the player has literally lifted, as when rearranging crew. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the held actor, written exactly as it appears on an actor.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the actor currently picked up on the cursor is of an actor type whose definition has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Unlike the reader that looks at the individual, this one asks about the kind of creature it is. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the held actor's actor type, written exactly as it appears on an actor type definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and yields its result, so the same piece of arithmetic can be written once and reused wherever it is needed. The caster, the target, the rank and the targeted tile all carry through, and a value written in brackets straight after the name becomes the letter x inside the shared formula. A name the game does not know reports an error and gives 0.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run.

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: The value the shared formula receives as its x. A whole number is used as written, the bare letter x passes on whatever value the calling formula was itself handed, and anything else is worked out as a formula first. Left out, the shared formula sees x standing at zero.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and clamps its result upward at zero, so a negative outcome comes out as 0. Use it where a shared piece of arithmetic may go negative but a negative contribution would be wrong, such as a bonus that should never become a penalty.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run before clamping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and clamps its result downward at zero, so a positive outcome comes out as 0. Only the negative part of the result survives, which is how you keep a shared piece of arithmetic to its penalty half.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run before clamping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and caps its result at 1, letting anything below that through unchanged including negatives. Use it to turn a shared count into an at-most-once contribution.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run before capping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and caps its result at -1, so anything above -1, zero and positive results included, comes out as -1. Only results already below -1 pass through unchanged.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run before capping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and caps its result at a number you choose, returning whichever is smaller. Use it to reuse a shared piece of arithmetic while holding it to a ceiling that suits this particular action.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run before capping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

arguments.name: ceiling
arguments.description: The highest value the operand can produce.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula and raises its result to a number you choose, returning whichever is larger. Use it to reuse a shared piece of arithmetic while holding it to a floor that suits this particular action.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run before clamping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

arguments.name: floor
arguments.description: The lowest value the operand can produce.

uses.description: Runs a named shared formula only when the caster knows a given support ability, and gives 0 otherwise. It is the compact way to write a bonus that a passive unlocks, without wrapping the whole thing in a separate condition. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
