arguments.description: The support ability the caster must know for the shared formula to run at all.

arguments.name: formulaGlobalID
arguments.description: The shared formula to run when the caster has the ability. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Runs one of the game's built-in calculations and yields its result. These cover the things a formula cannot easily work out for itself, from facing and line of sight to weather, time of day and the state of the fleet. A name the game does not recognise reports an error and gives 0.

arguments.name: mathOperator
arguments.description: Which built-in calculation to run.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: A number handed to the built-in calculation, for the ones that take a range, a limit or a count. A whole number is used as written; anything else is worked out as a formula first, and the letter x is not carried through here, so writing it yields zero. Left out, the value stands at zero, which most calculations read as no figure having been asked for; a calculation that ignores it behaves the same either way.

uses.description: Returns 1 when one of the game's built-in calculations comes out at exactly zero, otherwise 0. It is the compact way to test that a built-in condition does not hold, without wrapping the calculation in a separate comparison.

arguments.name: mathOperator
arguments.description: Which built-in calculation to run and test against zero. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Runs one of the game's built-in calculations and clamps its result upward at zero, so a negative outcome comes out as 0. Use it where a built-in figure may go negative but a negative contribution would be wrong.

arguments.name: mathOperator
arguments.description: Which built-in calculation to run before clamping. A bracketed value may follow the name to pass a number into it.

uses.description: Gives the target's overall damage multiplier against an element, found by multiplying together the multipliers of every element reaction the target has that responds to it. A target with no reaction to that element gives 1, and so does an operand evaluated with no target at all, which makes it safe to multiply straight into a damage formula. Resistances pull the figure below 1 and weaknesses push it above. This counts element multipliers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMultiplier), but not element multipliers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMultiplier).

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose reactions are gathered from the target.

uses.description: Adds up the flat damage adjustments from every element reaction the target has that responds to a given element. Each adjustment is worked out from its own formula and rounded down before being added. Unlike the multiplier reading, an absent target or a target with no such reaction gives 0, so this is meant to be added to a damage figure rather than multiplied into it. This counts element modifiers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMod), but not element modifiers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMod).

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose reactions are gathered from the target.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is outright immune to damage from an element, otherwise 0. Immunity means the target's reactions to damage from that element multiply out to zero or less, which is how the game expresses taking no damage at all. With no target the operand is 0. This counts element multipliers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMultiplier), but not element multipliers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMultiplier).

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element the target is tested for immunity to.

uses.description: Gives the caster's overall damage multiplier against an element, found by multiplying together the multipliers of every element reaction the caster has that responds to it. A caster with no reaction to damage from that element gives 1, and so does an operand evaluated with no caster at all. This counts element multipliers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMultiplier), but not element multipliers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMultiplier).

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose reactions are gathered from the caster.

uses.description: Adds up the flat damage adjustments from every element reaction the caster has that responds to a given element. Each adjustment is worked out from its own formula and rounded down before being added. An absent caster or a caster with no such reaction gives 0. This counts element modifiers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMod), but not element modifiers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMod).

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose reactions are gathered from the caster.

uses.description: Gives the target's overall multiplier against being hit with a particular actor value, found by multiplying together the multipliers of every reaction the target has to that actor value. Where the element-based reading asks about fire or lightning, this one asks about the thing being applied, such as poison or a stun. A target with no such reaction gives 1, and so does an operand evaluated with no target. This counts multipliers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMultiplier), but not multipliers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMultiplier).

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value whose reactions are gathered from the target.

uses.description: Adds up the flat adjustments from every reaction the target has to a particular actor value being applied to it harmfully. Each adjustment is worked out from its own formula and rounded down before being added. An absent target or a target with no such reaction gives 0, so this is meant to be added rather than multiplied. This counts modifiers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMod), but not modifiers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMod).

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value whose reactions are gathered from the target.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is outright immune to having a particular actor value applied to it harmfully, otherwise 0. Immunity means the target's reactions to that actor value multiply out to zero or less when harmful. Use it to ask whether a status such as poison or sleep would take hold at all. With no target the operand is 0. This concerns damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMultiplier), but not healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMultiplier).

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value the target is tested for immunity to.

uses.description: Gives the caster's overall multiplier against being hit with a particular actor value, found by multiplying together the multipliers of every reaction the caster has to that actor value. A caster with no such reaction gives 1, and so does an operand evaluated with no caster. This counts multipliers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMultiplier), but not multipliers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMultiplier).

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value whose reactions are gathered from the caster.

uses.description: Adds up the flat adjustments from every reaction the caster has to a particular actor value being applied to it harmfully. Each adjustment is worked out from its own formula and rounded down before being added. An absent caster or a caster with no such reaction gives 0. This counts modifiers to damage or actor values applied with a harmful magnitude (damageMod), but not modifiers to healing or actor values applied with a beneficial magnitude (healMod).

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: The actor value whose reactions are gathered from the caster.

uses.description: Counts how many separate element reactions the target has that respond to a given element. It counts entries, not their strength, so it answers how many different things would fire rather than how badly the target is hurt. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose reactions are counted on the target.

uses.description: Counts how many element reactions the tile this formula is being evaluated against would fire in response to a given element. This covers the ground itself and whatever is lying on it, so it is the way to ask whether a spot will catch fire, freeze or explode. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose reactions are counted on the targeted tile.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions written on an item's own definition that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches any reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to, so both fire and poison are sensible things to ask about. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose reaction list is searched.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives how many element reactions are written on an item's own definition, without filtering. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose reactions are counted.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions an item grants while it is wielded as a weapon that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches any reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose wielded-weapon reaction list is searched.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives how many element reactions an item grants while it is wielded as a weapon, without filtering. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose wielded-weapon reactions are counted.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions an item grants while it is worn as armour that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches any reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose worn-armour reaction list is searched.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives how many element reactions an item grants while it is worn as armour, without filtering. An item name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item whose worn-armour reactions are counted.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions built into a kind of creature that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches any reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to. An actor type name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type whose reaction list is searched.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives how many element reactions are built into a kind of creature, without filtering. An actor type name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorTypeID
arguments.description: The actor type whose reactions are counted.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions an actor class grants to whoever takes it that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches any reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to. An actor class name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose reaction list is searched.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives how many element reactions an actor class grants to whoever takes it, without filtering. An actor class name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actorClassID
arguments.description: The actor class whose reactions are counted.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions a support ability grants to whoever learns it that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches any reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to. A support ability name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability whose reaction list is searched.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives how many element reactions a support ability grants to whoever learns it, without filtering. A support ability name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability whose reactions are counted.

uses.description: Reads a global variable whose name is built by sticking a fixed prefix onto the contents of another global variable. It is the way to keep one record per subject, such as a per-town or per-character counter, and then look up whichever subject the story is currently pointing at. A name built this way that does not exist gives 0.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: Text placed in front of the other variable's contents to build the name to read.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose contents are appended to the prefix.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable whose name is built by sticking a fixed prefix onto the contents of another global variable stands at exactly 1, otherwise 0. Use it for per-subject flags, such as whether the town the story is currently pointing at has been visited. A name built this way that does not exist gives 0.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: Text placed in front of the other variable's contents to build the name to read.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose contents are appended to the prefix.

uses.description: Reads a global variable whose name is built by sticking a fixed prefix onto the ID of the place the player is currently at. It is the way to keep one record per port or settlement without naming each one. A name built this way that does not exist gives 0.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: Text placed in front of the current location's ID to build the name to read.

uses.description: Reads a global variable as a number. Global variables are the game's persistent record of what has happened, so this is the usual way for a formula to react to story progress. A variable that has never been set, or whose contents are text rather than a number, gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to read.

uses.description: Reads a global variable as a number and caps it at 1, so any positive value comes out as 1 while negatives pass through unchanged. Use it to turn a counter into a yes-or-no contribution without a separate comparison. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to read before capping.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable reads as zero, otherwise 0. A variable that has never been set also reads as zero, and so does one holding text rather than a number, so this passes for anything that has not been given a number.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to test against zero.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable stands at exactly 1, otherwise 0. This is the usual test for a story flag that has been switched on. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to test against 1.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable stands at exactly 2, otherwise 0. Useful for a flag with more than two states, such as a quest that is offered, accepted and then finished. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to test against 2.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds the ID of the actor the player is currently in conversation with, otherwise 0. Use it in dialog to recognise that the person being spoken to is the one the story has been keeping track of. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose contents are compared against the actor being talked to.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds the ID of the place the player is currently at, otherwise 0. Use it to recognise that the story's chosen port is the one the player has just sailed into. Away from any location, or with a variable that has never been set, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose contents are compared against the current location's ID.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds the faction that currently controls the place the player is at, otherwise 0. Since control can change hands, this tracks the present owner rather than the original one. Away from any location, or with a variable that has never been set, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose contents are compared against the current location's controlling faction.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds the faction of the actor the player is currently in conversation with, otherwise 0. Use it in dialog to react to who the speaker answers to. With nobody being spoken to, or a variable that has never been set, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose contents are compared against the speaker's faction.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds the ID of an actor in the current zone whose conversation starts at a given dialog node, otherwise 0. It is a way to confirm that the character the story has been tracking is present and is still the one running a particular conversation. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the actor ID to look for.

arguments.name: dialogNodeID
arguments.description: The dialog node that actor's conversation must start at.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the place named by a global variable has been discovered by the player, otherwise 0. Use it to hold back content about a port until the player has actually found it. A variable that has never been set, or one naming a place the game does not know, gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the ID of the place to check.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the place named by a global variable carries a given tag, otherwise 0. Tags are the loose labels a location can be marked with, such as what trade or terrain it is known for. A variable that has never been set, or one naming a place the game does not know, gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the ID of the place to check.

arguments.name: tag
arguments.description: The tag the place must carry, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds exactly a given piece of text, otherwise 0. It compares as text rather than as a number, so it works for variables that hold an ID or a name. A variable that has never been set reads as the text 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to read.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The text the variable must hold, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds exactly a given piece of text, otherwise 0, with the variable name and the expected text written together in one piece separated by a comma. This packed form exists because a colon cannot be used inside some places a formula is written. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarNameAndValue
arguments.description: The variable name and the expected text joined by a comma, as in questStage,accepted. The part before the comma is the variable, the part after it is the text it must hold.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds anything other than a given piece of text, otherwise 0. It compares as text rather than as a number. A variable that has never been set reads as the text 0, so it counts as different from anything else.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to read.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The text the variable must not hold, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds anything other than a given piece of text, otherwise 0, with the variable name and the rejected text written together in one piece separated by a comma. This packed form exists because a colon cannot be used inside some places a formula is written. A variable that has never been set gives 0 in this form, since the check also requires the variable to exist.

arguments.name: globalVarNameAndValue
arguments.description: The variable name and the rejected text joined by a comma, as in questStage,finished. The part before the comma is the variable, the part after it is the text it must not hold.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable reads as a number strictly below a given value, otherwise 0. A variable that has never been set, or one holding text, reads as zero. An exact match gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to read as a number.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The value the variable must fall below for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable reads as a number strictly above a given value, otherwise 0. A variable that has never been set, or one holding text, reads as zero. An exact match gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to read as a number.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The value the variable must exceed for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds text rather than a number, otherwise 0. A variable that has never been set gives 0, and so does one holding the text 0, which the game treats as the unset value. Use it to tell a variable that has been given a name or an ID from one that is just a counter.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable to inspect.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable holds the ID of the party member at a given position in the party order, otherwise 0. Positions are counted from zero, and a position past the end of the party gives 0. Use it to check that the character the story is tracking is in a particular slot.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable holding the actor ID to compare.

arguments.name: partySlot
arguments.description: Position in the party order to look at, counting from zero.

uses.description: Gives the moment on the world clock, in hours since the game began, at which a global variable was last given a value. Use it to work out how long ago something happened. A variable that has never been set gives 0.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose last assignment time is wanted.

uses.description: Gives how many world hours have passed since a global variable was last given a value. Twenty-four hours make a day. Returns 0 if the variable has never been set.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose last assignment is measured from.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a global variable was last given a value fewer than a given number of world hours ago, otherwise 0. Twenty-four hours make a day. A variable that has never been set gives 0, so this only passes for things that have actually happened recently.

arguments.name: globalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the global variable whose last assignment is measured from.

arguments.name: hours
arguments.description: The elapsed time must be below this many world hours for the check to pass.

arguments.name: prefix

Use it to ask whether two records point at the same thing, such as whether the port the player is heading for is the one a contract names. arguments.name: secondGlobalVarName
arguments.description: Name of the second global variable to compare.

uses.description: Reads how much of an element is lying on one specific map tile, named by its coordinates. Only that tile is read, the total is capped at 3, and nothing is shown on screen. Use it to probe a fixed spot regardless of what the formula is aimed at.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element whose strength is read from the tile.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column of the tile to read.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row of the tile to read.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the weapon in the caster's favoured hand has something slotted into it whose element matches the one given, otherwise 0. It looks at what has been fitted into the weapon rather than at the weapon itself, so it answers whether the blade has been tipped with fire, ice and so on. An empty hand, a weapon with no slot, or an empty slot all give 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element the slotted item must be of.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the weapon in the caster's favoured hand has something of a given element slotted into it and the caster is not already carrying a temporary enchantment of that same element, otherwise 0. The enchantment is recognised by the caster having a positive value in the actor value named after the element with Wpn added, such as fireWpn. Use it to stop a physical augment and a spell-granted enchantment from stacking.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element the slotted item must be of, and the one whose enchantment must be absent.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has been to a named zone during this session, otherwise 0. The game builds a map memory for a zone as the player enters it, and this asks whether that memory is currently loaded — loading a save starts that memory empty, so a zone visited in an earlier sitting reads as 0 until it is entered again. Use it to change what happens on a return visit within one sitting.

arguments.name: zoneID
arguments.description: The zone to ask about, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player is currently in a named zone, otherwise 0. Use it to make an effect or a piece of dialog specific to one place.

arguments.name: zoneID
arguments.description: The zone the player must currently be in, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the terrain under the target has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Without a target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and with neither the operand is 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a terrain type definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the terrain under the target is of a given element, otherwise 0. Without a target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and with neither the operand is 0. A name that is not a real element is read as no element at all, which then matches terrain that has no element.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: The element the terrain must be of.

uses.description: Counts the element reactions belonging to the terrain under the target that respond to a given element or to a given actor value. An element name matches a reaction listing that element; anything else is matched against the actor values a reaction responds to. Without a target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and with neither the operand is 0.

arguments.name: elementOrActorValue
arguments.description: An element name, or the name of an actor value a reaction responds to. Elements are recognised first; anything that is not one is taken as an actor value.

uses.description: Gives what percentage of a named zone's map the player has uncovered, from 0 to 100, worked out from how much of the zone's map memory is still fogged. The figure is rounded to two decimal places. A zone the player has never entered gives 0.

arguments.name: zoneID
arguments.description: The zone whose explored percentage is wanted.

uses.description: Counts the triggers in the current zone that cover the tile under the target and are presently able to fire. Naming an element narrows the count to triggers that respond to it; the element any counts them all. Without a target actor the tile being aimed at is used, and with neither the operand is 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: Only triggers that respond to this element are counted. Use any to count them regardless of element.

uses.description: Counts the triggers in the current zone that cover the tile under the target but are presently unable to fire, because their own conditions are not met. Naming an element narrows the count to triggers that respond to it; the element any counts them all. Without a target actor the tile being aimed at is used, and with neither the operand is 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: Only triggers that respond to this element are counted. Use any to count them regardless of element.

uses.description: Counts the triggers anywhere in the current zone that are presently able to fire, without regard to where they sit. Naming an element narrows the count to triggers that respond to it; the element any counts them all. Outside a zone the operand is 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: Only triggers that respond to this element are counted. Use any to count them regardless of element.

uses.description: Counts the triggers anywhere in the current zone that are presently unable to fire, because their own conditions are not met. Naming an element narrows the count to triggers that respond to it; the element any counts them all. Outside a zone the operand is 0.

arguments.name: element
arguments.description: Only triggers that respond to this element are counted. Use any to count them regardless of element.

uses.description: Counts how many effects a trigger carries. The trigger is found by its number within the current zone, or failing that by its name among the triggers shared across the whole game. Naming an effect narrows the count to just that kind. A trigger that cannot be found, or being outside a zone, gives 0.

arguments.name: triggerID
arguments.description: The trigger's number within the current zone, written as a plain number, or the name of one of the triggers shared across the whole game.

arguments.name: effectID
arguments.description: Restricts the count to effects of this kind. Leave it out to count all of the trigger's effects.

uses.description: Gives the longest delay set on any of a trigger's effects, which is how long after firing the last of them will have finished. The trigger is found by its number within the current zone, or failing that by its name among the triggers shared across the whole game. A trigger that cannot be found, or being outside a zone, gives 0.

arguments.name: triggerID
arguments.description: The trigger's number within the current zone, written as a plain number, or the name of one of the triggers shared across the whole game.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a trigger has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: triggerID

arguments.name: propertyName

arguments.name: value

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player is currently at a named place, otherwise 0. Out at sea, or anywhere that is not a location at all, the operand is 0. Use it to make dialog or an effect specific to one port.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place the player must currently be at, matched exactly.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property off a named place's record and yields it as a number. Any property whose text form parses as a number can be read this way. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose record is read.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a location record. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property off the record of the place the player is currently at. Out at sea, or anywhere that is not a location, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a location record. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has discovered a named place, otherwise 0. Use it to hold back content about a port until the player has actually found it. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place being tested.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place is currently available to be found, otherwise 0. As well as being marked discoverable, the place's own requirement must pass; that requirement is worked out with the party leader standing in as both caster and target and the place's map position as the tile. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place being tested.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named port has reached full wealth, meaning a wealth level of 100 or more, otherwise 0. Use it to gate the trade and shipbuilding a prosperous port can offer. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The port whose wealth is being tested.

uses.description: Counts how many of a given item a named place has for sale or in store, looking first at the shipwright's list of hulls, then at the place's stash, then at its cargo hold. A hull on the shipwright's list gives 1. An item stocked in unlimited quantity gives 9999. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose stock is searched.

arguments.name: itemTypeID
arguments.description: The item to look for. A ship type name matches against the shipwright's list of available hulls instead.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place is set up to spawn a given kind of encounter automatically, otherwise 0. This asks about the place's standing spawn list rather than about anything currently in the world. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose spawn list is searched.

arguments.name: spawnDataID
arguments.description: The spawn entry to look for on that list, matched exactly.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place is currently offering a quest of a given kind, otherwise 0. Naming a goal as well narrows it to a quest of that kind with that particular objective, which is how you ask whether the errand a port is offering is the specific one you care about. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose offered quests are searched.

arguments.name: questType
arguments.description: The kind of quest to look for, matched exactly against what the place is offering.

arguments.name: questGoal
arguments.description: Narrows the match to a quest of that kind whose objective is this. Leave it out to accept any goal.

uses.description: Gives the map column a named place sits at on the world map. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose column is wanted.

uses.description: Gives the map row a named place sits at on the world map. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose row is wanted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place shows a given icon in its map tooltip, otherwise 0. Those icons are how the map advertises what a port has on offer, so this is a way to ask whether that marker is currently up. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose tooltip icons are searched.

arguments.name: icon
arguments.description: Name of the icon to look for, matched exactly against the place's tooltip icon list.

uses.description: Gives how many separate item stacks a named place is holding in its stash, the store the player can leave things in. A stack of twenty counts as one. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose stash is measured.

uses.description: Gives how many separate item stacks a named place is holding in its cargo store, the goods it trades in. A stack of twenty counts as one. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose cargo store is measured.

uses.description: Gives how many hulls a named place's shipwright currently has on offer. A place the game does not know, or one with no shipwright, gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose shipwright list is measured.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place's stash has no free slots left, otherwise 0. Use it before an effect tries to put something into a port's store. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose stash is being checked for space.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place's cargo store has no free slots left, otherwise 0. Use it before an effect tries to add goods to a port's trade stock. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose cargo store is being checked for space.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place's shipwright already has its full complement of eight hulls on offer, otherwise 0. Use it before an effect tries to add another ship to a port's yard. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose shipwright list is being checked for space.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose record is inspected.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a location record.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Gives the player's standing with whichever faction currently controls a named place, never dropping below -99. Since control can change hands, this follows the present owner rather than the original one. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose controlling faction's standing is wanted.

uses.description: Gives how well a named faction stands with a named place, which is what decides whose ships are welcome in that port. A place that is sworn to its owner for good reports -9999 for any faction it has no recorded standing with, marking it as flatly unavailable rather than merely neutral. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose standings are read.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose standing with that place is wanted.

uses.description: Gives how many units of its trade good a named port produces in a day. Richer ports produce more, and cheaper goods are produced in greater numbers, so a poor port dealing in something valuable restocks slowly. The figure is never below 1, and a port at full wealth never below 2. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The port whose daily production is wanted.

uses.description: Gives what one serving of a named port's tavern food currently costs. This is the price for a single portion, not for feeding the crew. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The port whose tavern price is wanted.

uses.description: Gives what it would cost to feed the player's whole crew at a named port's tavern, one serving each. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The port whose tavern price is wanted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player can afford to feed the whole crew at a named port's tavern, otherwise 0. Having exactly the asking amount still counts as affordable. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The port whose tavern bill is compared against the player's purse.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named place has at least one ship among the things it can be persuaded to make available, otherwise 0. The place's unlock list can hold items as well as hulls, and only the hulls count here. A place the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: locationID
arguments.description: The place whose unlock list is searched for a ship.

uses.description: Gives the highest standing the player can currently reach with a named faction. It starts at 20 and rises by 10 for each rank the player holds, but only with the faction the player has actually sworn to, and it never passes 99. Use it to show how much room a reputation has left to grow.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose ceiling on standing is wanted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's total renown, the three strands of exploring, trading and fighting added together, is below a given number, otherwise 0. An exact match gives 0. Use it to keep early content from appearing once the player is well known.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The combined renown must fall below this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's total renown, the three strands of exploring, trading and fighting added together, is above a given number, otherwise 0. An exact match gives 0. Use it to unlock content once the player has made a name.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The combined renown must exceed this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Gives how many ports a named faction currently holds. Since control changes hands over the course of a game, this follows the present state of the map rather than how things started.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose ports are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named faction holds more than a given number of ports, otherwise 0. An exact match gives 0. Use it for content that turns on how far a power has spread.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose ports are counted.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The count must exceed this number for the check to pass.

uses.description: Gives how rich a named faction currently is, taken together across everything it holds. Use it for content that turns on whether a power is thriving or failing.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose wealth is wanted.

uses.description: Gives how many fleets a named faction currently has at sea, counting merchant convoys and war fleets alike.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose fleets are counted.

uses.description: Gives how many merchant convoys a named faction currently has at sea, leaving its war fleets out of the count. Use it for content about a power's trade rather than its navy.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose merchant convoys are counted.

uses.description: Gives how many war fleets a named faction currently has at sea, leaving its merchant convoys out of the count. Use it for content about a power's fighting strength.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose war fleets are counted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named faction has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list. A faction the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose definition is inspected.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a faction definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property straight off a named faction's definition and yields it as a number. Any property whose text form parses as a number can be read this way. A faction the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: factionID
arguments.description: The faction whose definition is read.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a faction definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Gives how much experience the party member at a given position has earned in the class they are currently training. Positions are counted from zero, and a position past the end of the party gives 0.

arguments.name: partySlot
arguments.description: Position in the party order to look at, counting from zero.

uses.description: Gives the lifetime experience of an actor in the current zone whose conversation starts at a given dialog node, which is how a trainer's or vendor's standing is judged. When several actors share that node the last one found wins. If nobody matches the operand is 0.

arguments.name: dialogNodeID
arguments.description: The dialog node an actor's conversation must start at for its experience to be read.

uses.description: Returns 1 when at least one actor in the current zone has its conversation starting at a given dialog node, otherwise 0. Use it to check that the character who runs a particular conversation is present before offering it.

arguments.name: dialogNodeID
arguments.description: The dialog node to look for among the actors in the zone.

uses.description: Counts how many actors in the current zone have their conversation starting at a given dialog node. Use it where more than one such character may be about and the number matters.

arguments.name: dialogNodeID
arguments.description: The dialog node to look for among the actors in the zone.

uses.description: Rolls a whole number between 0 and a given ceiling and returns 1 when it comes out equal to a value you name, otherwise 0. The roll is seeded from the target and from the current six-day stretch of world time, so it gives the same answer for the same target all week and then changes: it is how a character gets a stable but rotating mood, stock or greeting. Note that it also resets the value passed into the formula, so anything later in the same formula that uses x will see the ceiling instead. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: ceiling
arguments.description: The highest number the roll can produce; the roll runs from 0 to this value inclusive. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The rolled number must come out equal to this for the check to pass.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has recorded a given journal entry, otherwise 0. As well as a journal entry's own name it accepts the name of an item, an actor type or an actor class, and finds the entry that subject writes into. Use it to react to what the player has catalogued.

arguments.name: journalEntryID
arguments.description: The journal entry to look for. The name of an item, actor type or actor class is also accepted, in which case the entry it writes into is looked for.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has already sold or handed in a given journal entry, otherwise 0. This is about having cashed the discovery in, not merely having made it. As well as a journal entry's own name it accepts the name of an item, an actor type or an actor class.

arguments.name: journalEntryID
arguments.description: The journal entry to look for. The name of an item, actor type or actor class is also accepted, in which case the entry it writes into is looked for.

uses.description: Gives the rarity grade recorded on a journal entry, which is what decides how much a discovery is worth. As well as a journal entry's own name it accepts the name of an item, an actor type or an actor class. A subject with no journal entry at all gives -1, which is distinct from a real grade of 0.

arguments.name: journalEntryID
arguments.description: The journal entry whose rarity grade is wanted. The name of an item, actor type or actor class is also accepted.

uses.description: Gives what a journal entry pays out when it is handed in, being the standard reward for its rarity grade plus whatever adjustment that entry carries. As well as a journal entry's own name it accepts the name of an item, an actor type or an actor class. A subject with no journal entry, or one with no rarity grade, gives 0.

arguments.name: journalEntryID
arguments.description: The journal entry whose reward is wanted. The name of an item, actor type or actor class is also accepted.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a given goal is written into any of the player's fifty-four journal goal slots, otherwise 0. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing, so the goal need not be written exactly as it was recorded.

arguments.name: goal
arguments.description: The goal to look for among the recorded journal goals.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a given goal is written into one of the player's fifty-four journal goal slots and has been marked done, otherwise 0. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing. A goal that exists but is unfinished gives 0.

arguments.name: goal
arguments.description: The goal to look for among the recorded journal goals.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has written a given piece of text into one particular numbered line of the journal's notes page, otherwise 0. Lines are numbered from zero. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing, so the player need not have matched the spelling exactly.

arguments.name: noteLine
arguments.description: Which line of the notes page to look at, counting from zero.

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: The text that line must hold.

uses.description: Searches every line of the journal's notes page for a given piece of text and gives the number of the first line that holds it, counting from zero, or -1 when no line does. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing. Because a match on the very first line reads as 0, test for a result of -1 rather than for zero when you only want to know whether the player wrote it at all.

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: The text to search the notes page for.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named action has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list. An action the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action whose definition is inspected.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an action definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property straight off a named action's definition and yields it as a number. Any property whose text form parses as a number can be read this way. An action the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action whose definition is read.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on an action definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named support ability has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list. A support ability the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability whose definition is inspected.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a support ability definition.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Reads a numeric property straight off a named support ability's definition and yields it as a number. Any property whose text form parses as a number can be read this way. A support ability the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: supportAbilityID
arguments.description: The support ability whose definition is read.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read, written exactly as it appears on a support ability definition. Its value must read as a number.

uses.description: Gives what a named action costs to use, worked out with nobody in particular casting it. Because no caster is supplied, any part of the cost that depends on who is using the action or at what rank comes out as though those were zero, so this is the plain listed cost rather than the price for a specific character. An action the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action whose cost is wanted.

uses.description: Gives what a named action would cost the caster to use, worked out with the caster in place and at the rank the caster has bought in that action. With no caster, or an action the game does not know, the operand is -1, which is distinct from a genuine cost of 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action whose cost to the caster is wanted. The caster's value for an actor value of this same name is used as the rank.

uses.description: Gives what a named action would cost the target to use, worked out with the target in place and at the rank the target has bought in that action. With no target, or an action the game does not know, the operand is -1, which is distinct from a genuine cost of 0.

arguments.name: actionID
arguments.description: The action whose cost to the target is wanted. The target's value for an actor value of this same name is used as the rank.

uses.description: Returns 1 while the player is holding down the control bound to a named command, otherwise 0. Use it for abilities that react to the player still pressing the button. A command name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: command
arguments.description: Name of the bound command to check, as the game's controls list it.

uses.description: Gives how long the player has been holding down the control bound to a named command, in seconds. It reads 0 when the control is not being held. Use it for charged attacks and other abilities that build up while a button is down.

arguments.name: command
arguments.description: Name of the bound command to measure, as the game's controls list it.

uses.description: Gives how many times in quick succession the player has pressed the control bound to a named command. Use it to tell a single tap from a double or triple tap. A command name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: command
arguments.description: Name of the bound command whose press count is wanted, as the game's controls list it.

uses.description: Gives how long ago the player last pressed the control bound to a named command, in seconds. Use it for follow-up moves that only work within a window after an input. A command name the game does not know gives 0.

arguments.name: command
arguments.description: Name of the bound command whose last press is measured, as the game's controls list it.

uses.description: Tests for a well-timed button press during an attack and, when it lands, gives the caster's timed-hit power multiplier and plays the flash, dashes and whip-crack sound at the target. The press counts only if the caster has a timed-hit multiplier at all, the control bound to the named command is currently down but has been held for less than about a quarter of a second, it has not been pressed more than once, and the caster is either past the multi-press window in its animation or no longer busy. A miss gives 0.

arguments.name: command
arguments.description: Name of the bound command whose press is being timed, as the game's controls list it.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the item the cursor is currently over has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. This reads the individual item lying there, so it sees things like its quantity as well as what kind it is. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad. Properties that hold a list match when the value appears anywhere in the list.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the item under the cursor.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the item the cursor is currently over is of a kind whose definition has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Unlike the reader that looks at the individual item, this one asks about the kind of thing it is. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the item definition, written exactly as it appears on one.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the actor the cursor is currently over has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. This reads the individual character standing there, so it sees things like its faction and its current state. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the actor under the cursor.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the actor the cursor is currently over is of a kind whose definition has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Unlike the reader that looks at the individual actor, this one asks about the kind of creature it is. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the actor type definition, written exactly as it appears on one.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the terrain under the cursor has a given property set to a given value, otherwise 0. Height is ignored when working out which tile the cursor is over, so it picks the tile at ground level. Outside a loaded zone, or with the cursor off the play area, the operand is 0.

arguments.name: propertyName
arguments.description: Name of the property to read from the terrain type definition, written exactly as it appears on one.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The value the property must equal, or must contain if the property holds a list. Letter case and punctuation are smoothed out before comparing.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the cursor is hovering within a given number of tiles of a named map tile, otherwise 0. Height is ignored when working out which tile the cursor is over. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column of the tile to measure from.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row of the tile to measure from.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles away the cursor may be and still count.

uses.description: Gives how many tiles lie between the cursor and a named map tile, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. Height is ignored when working out which tile the cursor is over. With the cursor off the play area, or outside a loaded zone, the operand is -1.

arguments.name: tileX
arguments.description: Column of the tile to measure from.

arguments.name: tileY
arguments.description: Row of the tile to measure from.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the cursor is within a given distance in screen pixels of a fixed point on the screen, otherwise 0. This works in screen space rather than on the map, so it is for interface work rather than for anything in the world. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad.

arguments.name: screenX
arguments.description: Horizontal screen position to measure from, in pixels.

arguments.name: screenY
arguments.description: Vertical screen position to measure from, in pixels.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many pixels away the cursor may be and still count.

uses.description: Gives the straight-line distance in screen pixels between the cursor and a fixed point on the screen. With the cursor off the play area the operand is -1.

arguments.name: screenX
arguments.description: Horizontal screen position to measure from, in pixels.

arguments.name: screenY
arguments.description: Vertical screen position to measure from, in pixels.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named interface window is currently on screen, otherwise 0. The name may be either the window's own name or one of its aliases. Use it to make an ability or a piece of dialog depend on what the player has open.

arguments.name: windowName
arguments.description: Name of the window to look for, or one of its aliases.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the cursor is hovering over a named interface window, otherwise 0. Only visible windows count, and the name may be either the window's own name or one of its aliases. On a gamepad the cursor position follows the pad.

arguments.name: windowName
arguments.description: Name of the window the cursor must be over, or one of its aliases.

uses.description: Gives how far the cursor sits from the left edge of a named interface window, in screen pixels. It only reports while the cursor is actually over that window; at any other time the operand is -1. The name may be either the window's own name or one of its aliases.

arguments.name: windowName
arguments.description: Name of the window the position is measured within, or one of its aliases.

uses.description: Gives how far the cursor sits from the top edge of a named interface window, in screen pixels. It only reports while the cursor is actually over that window; at any other time the operand is -1. The name may be either the window's own name or one of its aliases.

arguments.name: windowName
arguments.description: Name of the window the position is measured within, or one of its aliases.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the cursor is within a given distance in pixels of a point inside a named interface window, otherwise 0. The point is measured from the window's own top left corner, so it stays put as the window moves. If the cursor is not over that window at all the operand is 0.

arguments.name: windowName
arguments.description: Name of the window the point sits in, or one of its aliases.

arguments.name: windowX
arguments.description: Horizontal position of the point, in pixels from the window's left edge.

arguments.name: windowY
arguments.description: Vertical position of the point, in pixels from the window's top edge.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many pixels away the cursor may be and still count.

uses.description: Gives the straight-line distance in pixels between the cursor and a point inside a named interface window, measured from the window's own top left corner. If the cursor is not over that window at all the operand is -1.

arguments.name: windowName
arguments.description: Name of the window the point sits in, or one of its aliases.

arguments.name: windowX
arguments.description: Horizontal position of the point, in pixels from the window's left edge.

arguments.name: windowY
arguments.description: Vertical position of the point, in pixels from the window's top edge.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the effect that landed just before this one was a given effect and it actually hit, otherwise 0. Use it to chain effects within a single action, so that a later part only applies when an earlier part connected. It does not care who cast that earlier effect.

arguments.name: sourceID
arguments.description: The ID of the effect definition that must have been the one that just hit.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the effect that landed just before this one was a given effect, it actually hit, and the caster was the one who applied it, otherwise 0. Use it to chain effects within a single action while ignoring anything another combatant did in between.

arguments.name: sourceID
arguments.description: The ID of the effect definition that must have been the one the caster just landed.

uses.description: Returns 1 when a named mod is installed and switched on, otherwise 0. The name may be either the mod's folder name or its display name with punctuation and spacing stripped out. A mod that is listed but whose folder is missing does not count. Use it to make content that adapts when another mod is present.

arguments.name: modName
arguments.description: The mod's folder name, or its display name with special characters removed.

uses.description: Reads an actor value from a fresh duplicate of the caster rather than from the caster itself. The duplicate is made at the moment the formula runs, so it carries whatever the caster has at that instant. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorValueID
arguments.description: Which actor value to read from the duplicate of the caster.

uses.description: Gives the distance in tiles between two named map positions, measured the way the game measures movement and reach rather than as a straight line. Both ends are given outright, so it does not depend on who is casting or what is being aimed at.

arguments.name: fromTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure from.

arguments.name: fromTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure from.

arguments.name: toTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure to.

arguments.name: toTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure to.

uses.description: Gives the distance in tiles between a named actor and a named map position, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. The actor is looked up among those present in the zone and in the fleets; if it is not there the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to measure from. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

arguments.name: toTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure to.

arguments.name: toTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure to.

uses.description: Gives the distance in tiles between the caster and a named map position, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: toTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure to.

arguments.name: toTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure to.

uses.description: Gives the straight-line distance between two named map positions, as the crow flies rather than as a figure walks. A diagonal therefore comes out longer than a step along a row. Both ends are given outright, so it does not depend on who is casting or what is being aimed at.

arguments.name: fromTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure from.

arguments.name: fromTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure from.

arguments.name: toTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure to.

arguments.name: toTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure to.

uses.description: Gives the straight-line distance between a named actor and a named map position, as the crow flies rather than as a figure walks. The actor is looked up among those present in the zone and in the fleets; if it is not there the operand is 0.

arguments.name: actorID
arguments.description: ID of the actor to measure from. A global variable name holding an actor ID is also accepted.

arguments.name: toTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure to.

arguments.name: toTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure to.

uses.description: Gives the straight-line distance between the caster and a named map position, as the crow flies rather than as a figure walks. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: toTileX
arguments.description: Column of the position to measure to.

arguments.name: toTileY
arguments.description: Row of the position to measure to.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the formula is being evaluated against an actual actor, otherwise 0. Use it to tell an attack aimed at a creature apart from one aimed at empty ground.

Returns 1 when the formula is being evaluated against an actual actor and that actor is not the caster, otherwise 0. Use it for effects that should only apply to somebody else, so a self-targeted use does not trigger them.
Returns 1 when the target is the actor whose turn it currently is, otherwise 0. Use it for effects that care about interrupting or rewarding whoever is presently acting.

Returns 1 when the caster and the target are the same actor, otherwise 0. Both must be present, so an action aimed at empty ground gives 0. Use it to give a self-targeted use of an action different numbers.

Returns 1 when the caster and the target are different actors, otherwise 0. Both must be present, so an action aimed at empty ground gives 0. Use it for effects that should not fire when someone targets themselves.
Returns 1 when the target is the character the player is controlling, otherwise 0. This picks out that one actor, not the player's side as a whole.
Returns 1 when the target belongs to the player's faction, otherwise 0. This covers the whole of the player's side rather than one particular character.
Gives how many tiles the player has picked out for the action being aimed. Use it for abilities that grow with the number of things they are being pointed at.
Gives how many of the tiles the player has picked out for the action being aimed actually have somebody standing on them. Empty ground in the selection does not count.

Returns 1 when the caster and the target share a map row or a map column, otherwise 0. In other words it asks whether they are lined up orthogonally, whatever the distance between them. Both must be present.
Returns 1 when the caster shares a map row or a map column with the tile being aimed at, otherwise 0. Unlike the actor-to-actor version this works for an action pointed at empty ground.

Gives how much of the caster's health is missing, as a fraction from 0 when unhurt to 1 when at nothing. Multiply it up for abilities that grow stronger as the caster is worn down. With no caster the operand is 0.

Gives how much of the target's health is missing, as a fraction from 0 when unhurt to 1 when at nothing. Use it for finishing moves that hit harder against a wounded foe. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the share of health the target has left has fallen to or below a figure you supply in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. The figure is a fraction, so 0.25 means a quarter of full health. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The share of full health to compare against, written as a fraction, so 0.25 means a quarter. Left out, the comparison is against zero, which only a target with no health left can meet.

uses.description: Gives a tenth of the target's undiminished maximum health, capped at 5. It scales an effect with how sturdy the target is meant to be rather than with how hurt it currently is, while keeping the figure small.

Returns 1 when the target has ten or less health left, otherwise 0. It is a fixed threshold rather than a share of the target's maximum, so it marks anything close to death regardless of how tough it is. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives nine tenths of the target's current health, so an effect using it takes the target most of the way down without finishing it. If nine tenths would leave less than two health behind it gives 0 instead, so the blow simply does nothing rather than killing. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives how much health the target lost to the last blow that landed on it, never below 0. Healing is reported as 0. Use it for retaliation and follow-up effects that mirror the damage just done. With no target, or a target no longer in the world, the operand is 0.

Gives how much health the target lost to the last blow that landed on it, but never more than it actually had at the time, and never below 0. This trims off the overkill on a killing blow, so a follow-up effect mirrors only the damage that really landed. With no target the operand is 0.
Gives how much health the caster lost to the last blow that landed on it, never below 0. Healing is reported as 0. Use it for counters and ripostes that pay back what the caster just suffered.

Gives how much health the caster lost to the last blow that landed on it, but never more than it actually had at the time, and never below 0. This trims off the overkill, so a counter mirrors only the damage that really landed. With no caster the operand is 0.

Gives how much health the target gained from the last thing that touched it, as a negative number, and 0 when the last thing was damage rather than healing. Because the figure comes out negative, an effect that wants to mirror a heal must flip its sign. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives how much health the caster had immediately before the last blow that landed on it, never below 0. Use it to work out how close a hit came to finishing the caster. With no caster the operand is 0.

Gives how much health the target had immediately before the last blow that landed on it, never below 0. Use it to work out how close a hit came to finishing the target. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the last blow that landed on the caster took more health than the figure you supply in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. An exact match gives 0. Use it for counters that only fire against a heavy hit.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The amount of health lost to compare against; the last blow must have taken strictly more than this. Left out, the comparison is against zero, so any damage at all counts.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the last blow that landed on the caster took less health than the figure you supply in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. An exact match gives 0. Use it for effects that reward shrugging off a glancing hit.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The amount of health lost to compare against; the last blow must have taken strictly less than this. Left out, the comparison is against zero, which no blow can come under.

uses.description: Gives how much health the caster lost to the last blow that landed on it, capped at the caster's life skill and never below 0. It is the usual shape for a healing riposte, where a stronger healer can undo more of what was just done.

Gives how much health the caster lost to the last blow that landed on it, capped at half the caster's life skill and never below 0. The cap is never less than 1, so even an unskilled healer recovers something.

Returns 1 when the last blow that landed on the caster took less health than half the caster's life skill, rounded down, plus one. It is the threshold form of a healing riposte: the check passes exactly when the caster could undo the whole of that damage.

Returns 1 when the last blow that landed on the caster took less health than half the caster's life skill, rounded down, plus two. It is a slightly more forgiving version of the same healing-riposte threshold.
