Returns 1 when the last blow that landed on the caster took less health than half the caster's life skill, rounded down, plus three. It is the most forgiving of the healing-riposte thresholds.
Returns 1 when the caster's magic points stand at exactly the figure you supply in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: mp
arguments.description: The magic point total the caster must be sitting at exactly. Left out, the test is for a caster with no magic points at all.

uses.description: Gives what the action the caster is presently casting or charging up will cost when it goes off, worked out at the rank and against the tile that queued action is actually aimed at. It only reports while the caster is mid-cast; at any other time the operand is 0. Use it for interrupts and counterspells that scale with what is being prepared.

Gives an evasion multiplier based on which way the target is facing relative to the caster, from 1 when it is looking straight at the attacker down to 0.1 when the attack comes from directly behind. The angle is settled to the nearest eighth of a turn first, giving 1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3 or 0.1. A target with no facing at all counts as fully alert and gives 1; an unconscious target, or a missing caster or target, gives 0.

Gives the facing-based evasion multiplier with the value a rear attack would earn already taken off, so a strike from directly behind comes out at 0 and one from the front at 0.9. Use it where an effect should scale with how much evasion the attacker has managed to strip away rather than with how much remains. An unconscious target, or a missing caster or target, gives 0; a target with no facing at all gives 1.

Gives the difference between the facing-based evasion multiplier as things stand and the multiplier the same attack would earn if the target were turned to face the other way. A frontal attack therefore comes out strongly positive and a rear one strongly negative, which makes it a measure of how badly the target is facing the wrong direction. An unconscious target, or a missing caster or target, gives 0; a target with no facing at all gives 1.

Gives how much physical evasion the target loses by being caught at an angle, capped at the target's own flanking-evasion allowance. It only produces a figure for a target that has such an allowance and is not being attacked head on; a target with no facing, an unconscious one, or a missing caster or target all give 0. Use it as the flanking bonus in a to-hit calculation.

Returns 1 when the target is facing the caster within an eighth of a turn either way, otherwise 0. A target with no facing at all never counts as front-facing. Use it for effects that only work on a foe that has seen you coming.

Returns 1 when the caster is behind the target, within a quarter turn either side of directly behind, otherwise 0. A target with no facing at all never counts as back-facing. Use it for backstabs and other effects that reward coming up from behind.

Gives the direction the caster is facing, as an angle in degrees from 0 to 359. It is settled to the nearest quarter turn, or to the nearest eighth for creatures that can stand on the diagonals. With no caster the operand is 0, which is also a real facing, so pair it with a separate check when that matters.

Gives the direction the target is facing, as an angle in degrees from 0 to 359. It is settled to the nearest quarter turn, or to the nearest eighth for creatures that can stand on the diagonals. With no target the operand is 0, which is also a real facing.
Returns 1 when the caster is on the hostile side, otherwise 0. Use it to give an action different numbers in enemy hands than in the player's.
Returns 1 when the caster is on the hostile side, otherwise 0. Use it to give an action different numbers in enemy hands than in the player's.
Returns 1 when the target is on the hostile side, otherwise 0. Use it for effects that should only bite enemies.
Returns 1 when the caster and the target are on the same side, otherwise 0. Use it to tell an ally from an enemy without naming factions. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the caster and the target are on opposite sides, otherwise 0. Use it to make an effect apply only to enemies without naming factions. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 while the caster is in motion, otherwise 0. It reads the actual movement happening on screen, so it is true during a step and false once the caster has settled. With no caster the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the caster is one of the actors the player can give orders to, otherwise 0. Use it to separate player-run characters from those the game moves on its own.
Returns 1 when the caster is of a humanoid kind, otherwise 0. Use it for effects that only make sense on people, such as equipment or morale rules. With no caster the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target is of a humanoid kind, otherwise 0. Use it for effects that only bite on people, such as fear or persuasion. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target cannot be killed, otherwise 0. Some story characters and set pieces are marked this way so that a fight with them cannot end badly. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target is a creature that can be tamed, is on the opposite side to the caster, and is still on its feet, otherwise 0. All three conditions must hold, which makes it the check to put on a taming ability. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target is of a kind that can be tamed at all, otherwise 0. Unlike the fuller check it does not care which side the target is on or whether it is still standing, so it answers what the creature is rather than whether taming would work now.
Returns 1 when the target is one of the actors the player can give orders to, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the caster and the target are alike in whether the player commands them, otherwise 0. Two player-run characters match, and so do two the game moves on its own. Both must be present.
Returns 1 when the target cannot be frightened, otherwise 0. Use it to stop a fear effect from being wasted on something that ignores it. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target is of a kind that cannot be brought back once it goes down, otherwise 0. Use it to keep a revival ability from offering itself where it would do nothing. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives how clever the target is, the figure the game uses to decide how well a creature reasons about a fight. Use it for effects that work better on dull-witted creatures than on sharp ones. With no target the operand is 0.
Gives how heavy the target's kind of creature is. Use it for shoves, throws and other effects that a heavier body should resist. With no target the operand is 0.
Gives the multiplier the game applies to the caster when weighing up how attractive a course of action is. It is part of how the computer-run side chooses what to do. With no caster the operand is 0.

Gives the multiplier the game applies to the target when weighing up how attractive a course of action is. Use it in the ratings that steer the computer-run side toward or away from particular victims. With no target the operand is 0.
Gives which of the two hand slots the target treats as its main hand, 0 for the first and 1 for the second. With no target the operand is 0, which is also a real slot.

Gives which of the two hand slots holds the target's off-hand weapon: 1 when the target favours the first slot, 0 when it favours the second. It is the mirror of the main-hand reading, so the two together name both hands. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the actor whose turn it currently is may take an action, otherwise 0. As well as the usual turn-order and interface rules this accounts for the zone forbidding action and for items on that actor's own tile that suppress acting, including ones that only do so in peaceful zones. It always asks about the current actor, not about the caster.
Returns 1 when the actor whose turn it currently is may move, otherwise 0. It always asks about the current actor, not about the caster.

Returns 1 when the actor whose turn it currently is may pick things up and put them down, otherwise 0. Unlike the similarly named check that takes an actor name, this one really does ask about handling items rather than about moving. It always asks about the current actor, not about the caster.
Gives the better of the caster's two ranged skills, bow and aim. Use it where an ability should work off whichever kind of shooting the character is actually good at.

Gives the weakest of the caster's five main melee weapon skills: sword, axe, hammer, spear and flail. Use it where an ability should be held back by a character's worst weapon rather than helped by its best.
Gives the weaker of the caster's two close-quarters skills, fist and dagger. Use it where an ability should be held back by whichever of the two the character has neglected.
Gives the weakest of the caster's six magic skills: fire, ice, lightning, wind, life and ruin. Use it where an ability should reward being rounded rather than specialised.

Returns 1 when the caster and the target share at least one actor class between their four class slots, or are simply the same kind of creature, otherwise 0. Empty class slots never match. Use it for kinship rules, where members of a profession or a species treat each other differently. Both must be present.

Returns 1 when the caster and the target share at least one actor class between their four class slots, otherwise 0. Unlike the wider version it does not accept merely being the same kind of creature. Empty class slots never match, and both actors must be present.
Returns 1 when the caster and the target are the same kind of creature, otherwise 0. Both must be present. Use it for effects that turn on facing one's own kind.

Counts how many pickable actor classes the caster currently qualifies for. Placeholder classes and ones the player cannot choose are left out, and each remaining class is tested against the caster's own entry conditions. With no caster the operand is 0.

Counts how many pickable actor classes the game defines in all, leaving out placeholders and any class the player cannot choose. Pair it with the count of known classes to show progress toward having seen them all.
Counts how many actor classes the player has discovered so far, leaving out placeholders. Pair it with the total number of classes to show progress toward having seen them all.
Returns 1 while a battle is under way, otherwise 0. Use it to give an ability different numbers in a fight than out of one.
Returns 1 while no battle is under way, otherwise 0. Use it for abilities meant for exploring and travelling rather than fighting.
Returns 1 when it is the caster's turn, otherwise 0. Outside a battle it always gives 1, since there are no turns to wait for. With no caster the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when a battle is under way and it is somebody else's turn, otherwise 0. Outside a battle it always gives 0. Use it for reactions and interrupts that only happen while the caster is waiting.
Returns 1 when the action presently being taken is a matter of handling items rather than fighting or moving, otherwise 0. Use it for rules that treat rummaging differently from combat.
Returns 1 when nothing has yet been done on the current turn, otherwise 0. Outside a battle it always gives 1. Use it for abilities that reward opening a turn with a particular move.
Returns 1 when something has already been done on the current turn, otherwise 0. Unlike its counterpart it does not treat being out of combat specially, so it simply reports 0 there.
Returns 1 when nothing was done on the previous turn, otherwise 0. Use it for abilities that build up while their owner holds back.
Returns 1 when movement has already happened on the current turn, otherwise 0. Use it for attacks that behave differently after a charge.
Returns 1 when no movement has happened on the current turn, otherwise 0. Outside a battle it always gives 1. Use it for abilities that reward standing still, such as aimed shots.
Returns 1 when no movement happened on the previous turn, otherwise 0. Use it for abilities that build up while their owner stays put.

Gives how many time ticks the target has progressed towards its next turn if it is participating in an ongoing battle, falling back to its total time required to act otherwise. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives how much of the target's wait is still to run before its turn comes round, falling back to its standing act time when it has no pending turn (i.e. is not participating in an ongoing battle). This is equivalent to substracting current m:tActTimer from the target's full actTime stat. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target's turn will come round in less than the figure you supply in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. A target with no pending turn is judged on its standing act time instead. Use it to decide whether a foe will get to act before something else resolves. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The amount of waiting time to compare against; the target's turn must come round in strictly less than this. Left out, the comparison is against zero, which no pending turn can beat.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the target is down, either marked as incapacitated or at no health left, otherwise 0. Use it to separate finishing and reviving effects from ones meant for a foe still standing. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target is in the middle of charging or casting something, otherwise 0. It is the check to put on an interrupt, so the ability only offers itself when there is something to break. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the caster is in a critical state, badly enough hurt that the game marks it as barely holding on, otherwise 0. With no caster the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target is in a critical state, badly enough hurt that the game marks it as barely holding on, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the caster is carrying at least one affliction that a general cure would lift, otherwise 0. To count, an effect must be of a kind that ordinary cures can remove, must actually be working against its owner, and must either be on a countdown or be one of the lasting kinds; being wet while drowning is specifically excluded. With no caster the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target is carrying at least one affliction that a general cure would lift, otherwise 0. To count, an effect must be of a kind that ordinary cures can remove, must itself allow such removal, must actually be working against its owner, and must either be on a countdown or be one of the lasting kinds; being wet while drowning is specifically excluded. With no target the operand is 0.

Counts how many harmful statuses the target is presently carrying that a general cure could lift. Only effects working against their owner count, long-term ones measured in days of world time are left out, and being wet while drowning is specifically excluded. Use it for effects that scale with how badly afflicted a foe is. With no target the operand is 0.

Counts how many statuses the target is presently carrying that a general cure could lift, helpful and harmful alike. Long-term effects measured in days of world time are left out, and being wet while drowning is specifically excluded. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives how long the target still has to wait before the thing it is casting or charging up goes off. It only reports while the target is actually mid-cast; at any other time the operand is 0. Use it to decide whether an interrupt would arrive in time.

Gives how much higher the caster's morale is than the target's, and 0 when the caster is not the more confident of the two. Use it for intimidation and rally effects that only work when the caster has the upper hand. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives the distance in tiles between the caster and the target, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. Supplying a figure in brackets after the name turns it into a check: it then gives 1 when the distance has reached that figure and 0 when it has not. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A distance to compare against; the operand is 1 when the target is at least this far away. Left out, the raw distance is returned.

uses.description: Gives the distance in tiles between the player's flagship and the target, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. Use it for world-map effects that turn on how far off a sail is. With no target, or no player flagship, the operand is 0.

Gives the straight-line distance between the caster and the target, as the crow flies rather than as a figure walks, so a diagonal comes out longer than a step along a row. Both actors must be present.

Gives how many tiles from the caster the effect being resolved has reached. It is set by the game as an area effect spreads outward, so it lets a blast fall off with distance from its centre. Outside such a spread it reports whatever the last one left behind.

Gives how far the caster has come from where it stood before it started moving, in tiles, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. If no move is in progress the operand is 0. Use it for charge attacks that hit harder the further they run.

Gives how many tiles have been walked so far on the current turn. Unlike the straight-line reading this counts the steps actually taken, so doubling back adds to it. Use it for abilities that spend or reward movement.

Gives the distance in tiles from where the caster stood before it started moving to the target, measured the way the game measures movement and reach. If no move is in progress it measures from where the caster is now instead. Use it for charges that care how far the victim was when the run began. With no target the operand is 0.

Counts everyone still on their feet within a number of tiles of the caster, friend and foe alike, including the caster itself. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name, and with none it counts only the caster's own tile. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the caster to search. Left out, the search covers the caster's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing enemies within a number of tiles of it. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name, and with none it looks only at the caster's own tile. Use it for abilities that reward or punish being surrounded. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the caster to search. Left out, the search covers the caster's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing enemies on the tiles immediately around it. The range is fixed at one tile, so no bracketed figure is needed. Use it to ask whether the caster is being pressed in close.

Counts the still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the caster that also belong to the caster's own faction, including the caster itself. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. Use it where only proper comrades should count, not every friendly creature on the field. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the caster to search. Left out, the search covers the caster's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of it, including the caster itself. Allegiance is judged by which side an actor is on rather than by faction. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the caster to search. Left out, the search covers the caster's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the target, including the caster itself if it stands that close. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the target, leaving the caster itself out of the count. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. Use it where an ability should reward having company rather than merely being present. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the target that also share a map row or column with it, so only those lined up orthogonally on the target count, including the caster itself when it stands that close and in line. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. With no caster the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the target that are carrying a melee weapon and could actually reach the target with it. The caster itself is included when it qualifies. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and the range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the target that are carrying a melee weapon and could actually reach the target with it, leaving the caster itself out. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and the range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. Use it for flanking bonuses that should count company rather than oneself.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing allies within a number of tiles of the target that are carrying a ranged weapon and could actually reach the target with it. The caster itself is included when it qualifies. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and the range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts everyone within a number of tiles of the target except the caster, friend and foe alike, and without regard to whether they are still standing. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's still-standing enemies within a number of tiles of the target, including the target itself when it is one. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. Unlike most of the near-target counts this one needs a real target actor rather than just a tile.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts everyone still standing on the tiles strictly between the caster and the target, walking straight from one to the other. Neither end is counted. Use it for shots and beams that weaken as they pass through a crowd. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Counts the caster's still-standing enemies within a number of tiles of the target that the action being aimed has not already picked out, and which are not the target itself. It answers how many more foes are in reach beyond the ones already caught. The range comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the target to search. Left out, the search covers the target's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts everyone standing on the target's own tile, whatever state they are in. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. Use it where several bodies can share a tile, as they can on a ship's deck.

Returns 1 when more than one actor is standing on the target's own tile, otherwise 0. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. Use it to catch the case where a tile is crowded.
Counts how many of the actors standing on the target's own tile are ones the player cannot command. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Counts how many of the actors standing on the target's own tile are currently in motion. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead. Use it to catch somebody passing through rather than standing there.

Counts how many of the tiles the game is currently highlighting green lie within one tile of the caster. Those highlights mark where the action being aimed can go, so this reports how many of them are right beside the caster. With no caster the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the tile being aimed at blocks effects from passing through it, otherwise 0. Sight is not considered, only whether an effect could carry on past. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the tile just short of the target, on the caster's side, is one the caster could not stand on, otherwise 0. Use it to tell whether a charge or a step-up to the target would be blocked before it arrives. Both a caster and a targeted tile are needed.

Returns 1 when the tile being aimed at is one an ordinary walker could stand on, otherwise 0. It is judged with the game's standard single-tile walking shape, so swimming, flying and other special movement do not count. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the tile just beyond the target, carrying on away from the caster, is one an ordinary walker could stand on, otherwise 0. Use it for shoves and knockbacks that need somewhere to push the victim into. Both a caster and a targeted tile are needed.

Returns 1 when the tile just beyond the target, carrying on away from the caster, lets effects pass through it, otherwise 0. Sight is not considered. Use it for attacks that continue past their victim. Both a caster and a targeted tile are needed.

Returns 1 when there is a clear path for both sight and effect from the caster to the tile being aimed at, otherwise 0. The path is traced as though airborne, so obstacles on the ground that a flying effect would clear do not block it. Both a caster and a targeted tile are needed.

Returns 1 when somebody is standing on the tile just short of the target, on the caster's side, otherwise 0. The caster itself does not count as being in its own way. Use it to tell whether a charge toward the target would run into someone first.

Returns 1 when somebody is standing on the tile just beyond the target, carrying on away from the caster, otherwise 0. The caster itself does not count. Use it for moves that carry through past the victim and need the far side clear.

Returns 1 when the tile just short of the target, on the caster's side, is either occupied by somebody or is one the caster could not stand on, otherwise 0. It combines the two ways a charge toward the target can be stopped before it arrives. The caster itself does not count as being in its own way.

Returns 1 when the tile just beyond the target, carrying on away from the caster, is either occupied by somebody or is one the caster could not stand on, otherwise 0. It combines the two ways a move that carries through past the victim can be stopped. The caster itself does not count.

Returns 1 when somebody other than the caster is standing on the tile directly beyond the target, carrying on away from the caster, otherwise 0. Diagonals count, so the line can run corner to corner. Use it for attacks that pass through and strike whoever is behind.

Returns 1 when one of the caster's allies is standing on the tile directly beyond the target, carrying on away from the caster, otherwise 0. Diagonals count. Use it to hold back an attack that would carry through into a friend.

Returns 1 when the target has a weapon in either hand that could be broken, otherwise 0. It runs the game's own breaking check without actually breaking anything, so unbreakable and already-broken weapons do not qualify. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target has something in its main hand that could be broken, otherwise 0. An empty hand, an already-broken item, or one marked unbreakable all give 0. With no target the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target has something in its off hand that could be broken, otherwise 0. An empty hand, an already-broken item, or one marked unbreakable all give 0. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the weapon the caster is currently using is broken, otherwise 0. An empty hand gives 0. Use it for penalties and repair prompts that only apply to a damaged weapon.
Returns 1 when either of the target's hands holds a broken item, otherwise 0. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target's main hand holds a broken item, otherwise 0. An empty hand gives 0, as does having no target.
Returns 1 when the target's off hand holds a broken item, otherwise 0. An empty hand gives 0, as does having no target.

Returns 1 when the target is wearing armour that could be broken, otherwise 0. It runs the game's own breaking check without actually breaking anything, so unbreakable and already-broken armour does not qualify. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target's armour slot holds a broken item, otherwise 0. An empty armour slot gives 0, as does having no target.
Counts how many broken items the caster is carrying. Containers in the inventory are not searched, so only what is directly held or worn is counted. With no caster the operand is 0.
Counts how many broken items the target is carrying. Containers in the inventory are not searched, so only what is directly held or worn is counted. With no target the operand is 0.
Counts how many broken items are sitting in the player's stash. Containers within the stash are not searched. Use it to prompt a trip to the smith.
Returns 1 when the target is holding something it could be made to drop, otherwise 0. It runs the game's own disarming check without actually dropping anything. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target is holding something in either hand, otherwise 0. It does not care whether the thing held is really a weapon. With no target the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target has something in its armour slot, otherwise 0. It does not care what state that armour is in. With no target the operand is 0.
Gives how much coin the target is carrying. Only the target's own top-level inventory is counted. With no target the operand is 0.
Gives what everything the target is carrying is worth, added together. Use it for pickpocketing and looting rules that scale with how rich a victim is. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives what it would cost to buy off the group the target fights with, worked out as a fraction of that group's fighting strength and rounded down. A tougher band demands more. It needs a target to work from.

Counts how many things fitted into the target's main-hand weapon actually do something while it is wielded, meaning they grant either an element reaction or an effect. Anything slotted in that does neither is not counted. An empty hand, something that is not a weapon, or a weapon with no slot all give 0.

Counts how many things fitted into the target's off-hand weapon actually do something while it is wielded, meaning they grant either an element reaction or an effect. Anything slotted in that does neither is not counted. An empty hand, something that is not a weapon, or a weapon with no slot all give 0.

Counts how many things fitted into the target's armour actually do something while it is worn, meaning they grant either an element reaction or an effect. Anything slotted in that does neither is not counted. An empty armour slot, something that is not armour, or armour with no slot all give 0.

Counts how many pieces of exclusive equipment the caster has on. Only the five main slots are examined: the two hands, which count only for weapons whose category is marked as applying to weapons, the armour slot, and the two accessory slots. An item with no exclusive category at all is not counted.

Counts how many pieces of exclusive equipment the target has on. Only the five main slots are examined: the two hands, which count only for weapons whose category is marked as applying to weapons, the armour slot, and the two accessory slots. An item with no exclusive category at all is not counted.
Gives how much coin the player has. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when the player has at least that much and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: An amount of coin to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for holding at least that much. Left out, the purse itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives how many characters are in the player's party. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when the party has at least that many and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A party size to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having at least that many. Left out, the count itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives how many characters are on the landing party, the group that goes ashore when the player leaves the ship. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when at least that many are ashore and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A landing-party size to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having at least that many ashore. Left out, the count itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives how many characters the player has in all, counting both the active party and everyone waiting in the barracks. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when there are at least that many and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A head count to compare against, covering the active party and the barracks together; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having at least that many. Left out, the count itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives the player's total renown, being the three strands of exploring, trading and fighting added together.
Gives how much renown in a single strand the player needs before the crown will offer its next commission. Pair it with the player's own renown to show how far off the next promotion is.

Returns 1 when the player's best single strand of renown has reached what the crown asks for its next commission, otherwise 0. Only the strongest of exploring, trading and fighting is compared, not the three added together.

Gives the player's standing with the faction the player has sworn to. Belonging to no recognised faction gives 0. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when the standing has reached that figure and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A standing to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having reached it. Left out, the standing itself is reported. Only figures above zero switch the check on, so a negative standing cannot be tested this way.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's standing with the faction the player has sworn to is below the figure supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Belonging to no recognised faction counts as a standing of 0. Use it where the check must work for negative thresholds too, which the combined reading cannot do.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The standing the player must be below. Left out, the comparison is against zero, so the check passes only while the player is already in disgrace with their own faction.

uses.description: Gives the player's standing with the faction the target belongs to. When there is no target it falls back to whoever the player is currently in conversation with, which is what makes it useful in dialog. A faction the game does not recognise gives 0.

Returns 1 when the player's standing with the target's faction has reached the figure supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Reaching it exactly still passes. When there is no target it falls back to whoever the player is currently in conversation with.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The standing the player must have reached with the target's faction. Left out, the comparison is against zero, so anything but a negative standing passes.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's standing with the target's faction is no worse than minus the figure supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Since a bracketed value cannot be written negative, this form exists to test how far into disgrace the player has fallen. When there is no target it falls back to whoever the player is currently in conversation with.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: How far below zero the standing with the target's faction may fall and still pass; the operand is 1 while the standing is no worse than minus this figure. Left out, the comparison is against zero, so anything but a negative standing passes.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's standing with the target's faction is below the figure supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. When there is no target it falls back to whoever the player is currently in conversation with.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: The standing with the target's faction the player must be below. Left out, the comparison is against zero, so only a negative standing passes.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's standing with the target's faction is worse than minus the figure supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Since a bracketed value cannot be written negative, this form exists to test how far into disgrace the player has fallen. When there is no target it falls back to whoever the player is currently in conversation with.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: How far below zero the standing with the target's faction must have fallen; the operand is 1 once it is worse than minus this figure. Left out, the comparison is against zero, so only a negative standing passes.

uses.description: Gives how strong the player's party is reckoned to be, counting the equipment and buffs they currently have. Use it to scale encounters and prices to how formidable the party has become.

Gives how strong the player's party is reckoned to be before their gear and temporary advantages are counted, so it measures the characters themselves rather than what they are carrying. Use it where scaling should follow progress rather than loot.

Gives how strong the hostile side in the current zone is reckoned to be, adding up every enemy present plus whatever is still in the middle of being spawned. Use it to judge the weight of the opposition.

Gives how the player's strength compares to the opposition's, as the party's power divided by the enemy's. Above 1 means the party has the advantage and below 1 means it is outmatched. With no enemies present at all the operand is 0. The party side is measured before gear is counted, so a well-equipped party reads lower than it plays.
Counts how many journal entries the player has recorded that carry a rarity grade. Entries with no grade, such as the help pages, are left out. Use it to measure progress through the catalogue.
Counts how many journal entries the player has already sold or handed in. It measures discoveries cashed in rather than discoveries made.
Counts how many of the player's fifty-four journal goal slots hold a goal that has not yet been marked done. Use it to show how much is still outstanding.
Counts how many of the player's fifty-four journal goal slots hold a goal that has been marked done. Use it to show how much has been achieved.
Counts how many lines of the journal's notes page the player has actually written something on. Blank lines are not counted.

Gives what the museum display in the current zone is worth, being the sum over each museum tile of the most valuable exhibit standing on it. A tile with several things on it counts only its best piece, so crowding a tile adds nothing. Value is reckoned from each exhibit's journal reward.

Counts the rare journal entries the player has recorded but not yet handed in, leaving out the help pages. Only entries above the third rarity grade count as rare. Supplying a figure in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when there are at least that many and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A number of discoveries to compare against; supplying one turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for holding at least that many. Left out, the plain count is reported.

uses.description: Counts the kinds of creature the player has killed that have a journal entry to be earned but which the player has not yet recorded. Use it to prompt the player to write up what they have been fighting.
Gives how much cargo the player's fleet is presently carrying. Pair it with the capacity to work out how full the holds are.
Gives how much cargo the player's fleet can carry in all. Pair it with the current load to work out how full the holds are.
Gives how much room is left in the player's holds. Supplying a figure in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when at least that much room remains and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: An amount of hold space to compare against; supplying one turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having at least that much free. Left out, the free space itself is reported.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player's fleet is carrying more than its holds can properly take, otherwise 0. Being overloaded slows a ship down, so this is the check to put on the penalty.

Gives how many rations the player could buy right now, being whichever is smaller of what the purse will stretch to at the current price and what the holds have room for. Use it to fill in the largest sensible quantity on a buying prompt.
Gives how much damage the player's fleet is carrying that a shipwright could put right. Use it to decide whether repairs are worth offering at all.
Gives what repairing the player's fleet would cost here, with any discount the player's standing earns already applied. Use it for the price actually quoted to the player.
Gives what repairing the player's fleet would cost before any discount the player's standing earns. Pair it with the discounted price to show what the player's reputation is saving them.

Returns 1 when the player can afford the number of rations supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. It prices them at the food's flat listed worth rather than at what this port is charging. Without a bracketed figure the operand is always 0.

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.description: How many rations to price up. Left out, the operand is always 0, since nothing is being bought.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player can afford the number of units of the local trade good supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. The good is the one the port covering the current zone deals in, priced at its flat listed worth rather than at what the port is charging. Without a bracketed figure the operand is always 0.

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.description: How many units of the local trade good to price up. Left out, the operand is always 0, since nothing is being bought.

uses.description: Returns 1 when any ship in the player's fleet carries two of the same thing in its own inventory, otherwise 0. Only plain items are remembered for the comparison; anything that grants an effect or an element reaction is skipped, so two identical enchanted pieces do not trip it. Use it to warn about a wasteful loadout.

Returns 1 when none of the player's ships have anything fitted at all while there is at least one weapon sitting in the hold, otherwise 0. It is the prompt for a player who has bought guns but not mounted them.

Returns 1 when the caster's ship has somebody aboard who could lead a boarding action, otherwise 0. A ship the player commands always qualifies; otherwise at least one of the first five crew must still be on their feet. A caster with no crew at all gives 0.
Returns 1 when the caster is a ship rather than a person, otherwise 0. Use it to separate the sailing rules from the land ones on a shared action. With no caster the operand is 0.
Returns 1 when the target is a ship rather than a person, otherwise 0. Use it for effects that only make sense against a hull. With no target the operand is 0.

Gives the recorded worth of one of the player's ships, picked by its position in the fleet, counting from zero. The position comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. Only ships still afloat are counted, and a position past the end of the fleet gives 0.

arguments.name: fleetIndex
arguments.description: Which of the player's ships to read, counting from zero along the fleet. Left out, the first ship is read.

uses.description: Gives how many rations the player's people get through in a day. Use it to work out how long the current stores will last.

Gives how many hands the player's fleet has in all, counting everyone aboard whatever state they are in. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when there are at least that many and 0 when not. With no player fleet the operand is 0.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A crew count to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having at least that many hands. Left out, the head count itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives the effective crew strength of the player's fleet, the count the game uses for working ships rather than a plain head count. With no player fleet the operand is 0.

Gives how many hands are aboard one of the player's ships, picked by its position in the fleet, counting from zero. The position comes from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. Everyone counts here, including the wounded and the unconscious. A position past the end of the fleet gives 0.

arguments.name: fleetIndex
arguments.description: Which of the player's ships to read, counting from zero along the fleet. Left out, the first ship is read.

uses.description: Gives how many hands the caster's kind of ship needs to work properly. Falling below it slows the vessel down, so pair it with the actual crew count to see whether the ship is undermanned.

Gives the effective crew strength aboard the caster's ship: how many hands it has that are still on their feet. Crew who are down or drowning do not count at all, and badly wounded crew count as half a person, so the result can come out on a half.

Gives the effective crew strength aboard the caster's ship, capped at the figure supplied in brackets after the name. Use it where extra hands stop helping past a certain point. Without a bracketed figure the cap is zero, so the operand comes out at 0 or less.

arguments.name: cap
arguments.description: The largest crew figure the operand will report, so hands past this point stop counting. Left out, the cap is zero and the operand never rises above 0.

uses.description: Gives a multiplier that falls as the caster's ship runs short of hands: 1 while it is adequately crewed, 0.75 with one hand or less, and 0.5 with half a hand or less. A vessel that needs no more than one crewman always gives 1. Multiply an effect by it to have a skeleton crew weaken the ship's work.

Gives the effective crew strength aboard the target's ship: how many hands it has that are still on their feet. Crew who are down or drowning do not count at all, and badly wounded crew count as half a person.

Gives the morale of the caster's crew as a fraction from 0 to 1. For a ship the player commands it follows the player's own crew morale; every other ship is treated as sitting at 0.7. Multiply an effect by it to have unhappy crews work less well.
Gives the morale of the player's own crew as a fraction from 0 to 1. Unlike the caster-based reading it always reports the player's crew, whoever is acting.
Returns 1 when at least one of the caster's crew is still on their feet, otherwise 0. Badly wounded crew still count as present here, unlike in the effective-strength reading.
Returns 1 when none of the caster's crew are still on their feet, otherwise 0. Use it to catch a ship that has been left crewless.
Gives the player's crew morale on its own scale of 0 to 100, rather than as a fraction. Use it where the figure is being shown to the player rather than multiplied into something.

Gives how many ships the player still has afloat, leaving out any that have been sunk or disabled. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 when the fleet is strictly larger than that figure and 0 when not. With no player fleet the operand is 0.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A fleet size to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having strictly more ships than that. Left out, the number of ships itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives how many ships the target's fleet still has afloat, leaving out any that have been sunk or disabled. With no target, or a target that sails alone, the operand is 0.
Gives how many ships are on the roster of the target's fleet, counting sunk and disabled ones as well as those still afloat. With no target, or a target that sails alone, the operand is 0.

Gives how many separate item stacks are stowed in the target's fleet's shared hold. A stack of twenty counts as one, so this measures how full the hold is rather than how much is in it. With no target, or a target that sails alone, the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the player's fleet outmatches the fleet of whoever the player is currently in conversation with, otherwise 0. The other side's strength is tripled and then scaled by how brave its commander is before the comparison, so a bold captain holds his nerve against much longer odds. It is the check behind whether a hail turns into a surrender.

Returns 1 when the player's fleet outmatches the caster's own fleet, otherwise 0. The caster's side is tripled and then scaled by how brave the caster is before the comparison, so a bold captain holds his nerve against much longer odds. Use it for decisions the other side makes about whether to fight.

Gives how fast the player is presently moving over the ground, taking the terrain underfoot into account. A player standing idle with no movement being asked for gives 0. Use it for effects that turn on being under way.
Returns 1 when the target sails with a merchant convoy rather than a war fleet, otherwise 0. Use it to treat traders differently from warships. A target that sails alone gives 0.
Returns 1 when the target sails with an elite fleet, the tougher and better-equipped kind, otherwise 0. A target that sails alone gives 0, as does having no target.

Gives the total weight resting on the tile being aimed at, adding up everyone standing there and everything lying there. Use it for floors and bridges that give way under a load. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

Counts the buried items on the tile being aimed at, leaving out things that are always buried by their nature. It therefore reports what could actually be dug up. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the tile being aimed at has anything overhead acting as a roof, otherwise 0. Use it for weather and falling effects that only reach the open air. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.
Gives the red part of the current zone's darkness tint, from 0 to 255. It reports how the zone is lit as a whole rather than how bright any one tile is. Outside a loaded zone the operand is 0.
Gives the green part of the current zone's darkness tint, from 0 to 255. It reports how the zone is lit as a whole rather than how bright any one tile is. Outside a loaded zone the operand is 0.
Gives the blue part of the current zone's darkness tint, from 0 to 255. It reports how the zone is lit as a whole rather than how bright any one tile is. Outside a loaded zone the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the target's tile is genuinely in the dark, otherwise 0. All of the following must hold: the zone is a dark one, its darkness tint is deep enough to matter, and no light is falling on that tile. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Gives the red part of the light falling on the target's tile, from 0 to 255. In a zone that is not dark it always reads as full. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and outside a loaded zone the operand is 0.

Gives the green part of the light falling on the target's tile, from 0 to 255. In a zone that is not dark it always reads as full. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and outside a loaded zone the operand is 0.

Gives the blue part of the light falling on the target's tile, from 0 to 255. In a zone that is not dark it always reads as full. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and outside a loaded zone the operand is 0.

Gives the three parts of the light falling on the target's tile added together, so it runs from 0 in pitch darkness to 765 in full light. In a zone that is not dark it always reads as full. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Gives how dark the target's tile is as a percentage, where 0 is as bright as the zone gets and 100 is as dark as the zone's own tint allows. It is measured against the zone's own darkness rather than against absolute black, so a dim zone still reports 0 where its lamps reach. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Gives how well lit the target's tile is as a percentage, where 100 is as bright as the zone gets and 0 is as dark as the zone's own tint allows. It is the complement of the darkness reading. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Gives how high the target's tile stands. Use it for rules about attacking uphill or downhill, or for effects that need the ground level. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead.

Returns 1 when the tile being aimed at is still hidden under the map's fog, meaning the player has never seen it, otherwise 0. Tiles outside the zone's bounds do not count as fogged. Without a targeted tile the operand is 0.

Gives what percentage of the current zone's map the player has uncovered, from 0 to 100, worked out from how much of the zone's map memory is still fogged. The figure is rounded to two decimal places.
Returns 1 when the current zone is the world map rather than a place the player has landed in, otherwise 0. Use it to separate sailing rules from shore rules.
Returns 1 when the current zone is marked peaceful, meaning fighting is not meant to happen there, otherwise 0. Use it to hold back aggressive abilities in a town.
Gives which weather is currently in force, as the number of that weather in the game's own list. Compare it against a fixed number to test for a particular kind of weather.
Gives which way the wind is blowing, as an angle in degrees. Pair it with a ship's facing to work out whether it is sailing with the wind or against it.
Gives how many tiles wide the current zone is. Use it for effects that scale with the size of the map.
Gives how many tiles tall the current zone is. Use it for effects that scale with the size of the map.

Counts how many element reactions the terrain under the target has in all, without filtering by element. When there is no target actor the tile being aimed at is used instead, and with neither the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the player is at a port, otherwise 0. On the world map, where the player is not at a location as such, it instead looks for a port within four tiles and reports whether one is there. Use it to offer harbour services.

Gives how prosperous the place the player is at has become, on the game's wealth scale. On the world map, where the player is not at a location as such, it looks for a port within four tiles and reports that one instead. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check: it then gives 1 when the wealth has reached that figure and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A wealth level to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having reached it. Left out, the wealth level itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives the player's standing with whichever faction controls the place the player is at, never dropping below -99. On the world map it looks for a port within four tiles and uses that one's owner instead. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check: it then gives 1 when the standing has reached that figure and 0 when not.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A standing to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for having reached it. Left out, the standing itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives how many units of its trade good the port the player is at produces in a day. Richer ports produce more, and cheaper goods are produced in greater numbers, so a poor port dealing in something valuable restocks slowly. The figure is never below 1, and a port at full wealth never below 2. Away from any location the operand is 0.

Gives what one serving of the local tavern's food currently costs at the place the player is at. This is the price for a single portion, not for feeding the crew. Away from any location the operand is 0.
Gives what it would cost to feed the player's whole crew at the local tavern where the player is at. Away from any location the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the player can afford to feed the whole crew at the local tavern where the player is at, otherwise 0. Having exactly the asking amount still counts as affordable. Away from any location the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the place the player is at has at least one ship among the things it can be persuaded to make available, otherwise 0. The unlock list can hold items as well as hulls, and only the hulls count here. Away from any location the operand is 0.

Returns 1 when the place the player is at lies west of the world-map column supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Use it to divide the map into regions for content that belongs to one part of the world. Away from any location the operand is 0.

arguments.name: column
arguments.description: The world-map column the place must lie west of. Left out, the comparison is against column zero, which nothing can be west of.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the place the player is at lies north of the world-map row supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Use it to divide the map into regions for content that belongs to one part of the world. Away from any location the operand is 0.

arguments.name: row
arguments.description: The world-map row the place must lie north of. Left out, the comparison is against row zero, which nothing can be north of.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the place the player is at lies east of the world-map column supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Use it to divide the map into regions for content that belongs to one part of the world. Away from any location the operand is 0.

arguments.name: column
arguments.description: The world-map column the place must lie east of. Left out, the comparison is against column zero, so everywhere but the westernmost column passes.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the place the player is at lies south of the world-map row supplied in brackets after the name, otherwise 0. Use it to divide the map into regions for content that belongs to one part of the world. Away from any location the operand is 0.

arguments.name: row
arguments.description: The world-map row the place must lie south of. Left out, the comparison is against row zero, so everywhere but the northernmost row passes.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the place the player is at is one where allegiance can be sworn or renounced, otherwise 0. Away from any location the operand is 0. Use it to offer the option only where it is available.

Returns 1 when today is the day of the week picked by the figure supplied in brackets after the name, counting from zero through the game's own list of day names, otherwise 0. Use it for shops and events that keep a weekly rhythm.

arguments.name: dayIndex
arguments.description: Which day of the week to test for, counting from zero along the game's list of six day names. Left out, the first day of the week is tested. A figure past the last day is an error.

uses.description: Returns 1 during the day and 0 at night. Use it for creatures, shops and events that keep to one or the other.

Gives the reading on the world clock in hours since the game began, counting up without ever wrapping round. Twenty-four hours make a day. Use it for measuring elapsed time rather than for telling the time of day.
Gives the day of the month, from 1 to 30. Supplying a figure above zero in brackets after the name turns it into a check instead: it then gives 1 once the month has reached that day and 0 before.

arguments.name: threshold
arguments.description: A day of the month to compare against; supplying one above zero turns the operand into a yes-or-no check for the month having reached that day. Left out, the day of the month itself is reported.

uses.description: Gives which month of the year it currently is. Use it for seasonal content.
Gives how many days have passed since the game began, counting the first day as 1 and never wrapping round at the end of a month. Use it for measuring how long a voyage has been going on.
Gives how long the player has spent in this save, in real time rather than world time. Use it for milestones that reward time at the keyboard.

Gives how long the game has been running since it was started, in real time. Unlike the play-time reading it resets when the game is closed, which makes it useful for timing animations and effects on screen.
Returns 1 when the effect that landed just before this one actually hit, otherwise 0. Unlike the named versions it does not care which effect that was. Use it to chain effects within a single action.

Returns 1 when the effect that landed just before this one passed its chance roll, otherwise 0. Passing the roll is not the same as connecting, so an effect can pass its chance and still be shrugged off. Use it to chain effects that should follow the roll rather than the outcome.

Turns whatever chance the effect being resolved has over 100 into a bonus multiplier, capped at 0.3 and never below 0. An effect certain to land at exactly 100 gives 0, and one at 150 gives 0.3. Use it to let overwhelming accuracy convert into extra damage instead of being wasted.

Rolls a whole number between 0 and the ceiling supplied in brackets after the name, inclusive at both ends. A ceiling below 1 is treated as 1, so the smallest roll is a coin toss between 0 and 1. It rolls afresh every time it is worked out.

arguments.name: maximum
arguments.description: The highest number the roll can come up with; the roll runs from 0 to this figure and both ends can come up. Left out, it is treated as 1, giving a coin toss between 0 and 1.

uses.description: Gives 1 or -1 at random, an even chance of each. Multiply a value by it to send an effect one way or the other, such as a shove to left or right.

Rolls a whole number between 0 and the ceiling supplied in brackets after the name, seeded from the target so that the same target always gives the same answer. A ceiling below 1 is treated as 1. Use it to give a character a stable quirk, greeting or stock that does not change from one look to the next. With no target the operand is 0.

arguments.name: maximum
arguments.description: The highest number the roll can come up with; the roll runs from 0 to this figure and both ends can come up. Left out, it is treated as 1, giving a coin toss between 0 and 1.

uses.description: Returns 1 when the player has unlocked the extra playable races, otherwise 0. Use it to gate content that only makes sense once they are available.
Returns 1 while the game is running in ruin mode, otherwise 0. Use it for content that only belongs in that mode.
Counts how many items the player has currently picked up on the cursor, adding up stack quantities. Nothing held gives 0.
Returns 1 when the player has an actor picked up on the cursor, as when rearranging crew, otherwise 0.
Gives how long the player has been holding the item currently picked up on the cursor, in seconds. Use it for interface effects that build up while something is lifted.
Gives how long ago the player last put down something they were holding, in seconds. Use it for interface effects that fade after a drop.

Returns 1 when the player is playing with a gamepad, otherwise 0. It counts both a pad set as the preferred device and a pad that simply happened to be used last, so it follows what the player is actually holding.
Gives the map column of the tile the action currently being carried out was pointed at. It is set as the action runs, so it lets a later step refer back to where the whole thing was aimed.
Gives the map row of the tile the action currently being carried out was pointed at. It is set as the action runs, so it lets a later step refer back to where the whole thing was aimed.
Returns 1 while a cutscene is playing, otherwise 0. Use it to hold back interface elements and abilities during a scripted scene.
Returns 1 when the game would presently allow the player to save, otherwise 0. Use it to offer or grey out a save option at the right moments.
Returns 1 when the game is presently accepting orders from the player, otherwise 0. It goes down during animations, cutscenes and the other side's turns.
Gives how many characters the player may take in the active party at once. Pair it with the current party size to tell whether there is room for another.
Gives how far the view is currently zoomed in. Use it for interface work that must size itself to the current zoom.
Gives the cursor's horizontal position on screen, in pixels. With the cursor off the play area the operand is -1. On a gamepad the position follows the pad.
Gives the cursor's vertical position on screen, in pixels. With the cursor off the play area the operand is -1. On a gamepad the position follows the pad.
Gives the map column of the tile the cursor is hovering over. Height is ignored when working out which tile that is. With the cursor off the play area the operand is -1.
Gives the map row of the tile the cursor is hovering over. Height is ignored when working out which tile that is. With the cursor off the play area the operand is -1.
Gives how far the cursor has moved horizontally since the last moment the game looked, in pixels. Use it for interface work that reacts to dragging.
Gives how far the cursor has moved vertically since the last moment the game looked, in pixels. Use it for interface work that reacts to dragging.
Gives how far the scroll wheel has turned since the last moment the game looked, positive one way and negative the other. Use it for interface work that reacts to scrolling.
Returns 1 while the game is running with debug mode switched on, otherwise 0. Use it to show diagnostics that ordinary players should never see.
Returns 1 while the game is running fullscreen, otherwise 0. Use it for interface layout that must differ between fullscreen and a window.
Returns 1 when the player has chosen borderless fullscreen rather than the exclusive kind, otherwise 0.
Returns 1 when the player has left the intense visual effects switched on, otherwise 0. Use it to hold back flashing and shaking for players who have turned those off.
Returns 1 when the player has switched on the colourblind adjustments, otherwise 0. Use it to pick shapes and markings over colour alone.
Returns 1 when the player has switched on the dyslexia-friendly typeface, otherwise 0. Use it where a layout must make room for different lettering.
Returns 1 when the player has switched on the retro visual style, otherwise 0.
Gives the player's overall volume setting. Use it for effects that should scale with how loud the player wants the game.
Gives the player's sound effects volume setting, separately from music and from the overall level.
Gives the player's music volume setting, separately from sound effects and from the overall level.

Gives which combat difficulty the player has chosen, as a step from 1 for the easiest to 5 for the hardest. A setting that matches none of the five recognised steps gives 0, which can happen when the difficulty has been altered outside the usual choices.
Gives which enemy thinking-speed setting the player has chosen, as a step from 1 for the most deliberate to 4 for the quickest. A setting that matches none of the four recognised steps gives 0.
Gives the player's chosen travel and survival difficulty, the setting that governs how harsh voyaging is. Use it to scale food, morale and weather rules.
Gives the raw multiplier the chosen combat difficulty applies to enemy statistics. Unlike the stepped difficulty reading this is the actual number the game multiplies by.
Gives the adjustment the current settings apply to how strong spawned enemies are. Use it where content must account for the player having made encounters harder or easier.
Gives the extra movement the current settings grant the player's characters. Use it where content must account for the player having made travel easier or harder.
Gives the raw adjustment the chosen setting makes to how long the computer-run side may take over a turn. Unlike the stepped reading this is the actual number the game applies.
Gives the adjustment applied to how good a plan must look before the computer-run side will commit to it. Raising it makes enemies pickier about what they will do.
Returns 1 when the player is playing under the stricter saving rules, where saving is only allowed in port, otherwise 0. Note that it reports the restriction rather than the permission.
Gives the multiplier the current settings apply to experience the player earns. Use it where content must account for a faster or slower advancement setting.
Returns 1 when the player has timed hits switched on, otherwise 0. Use it to hold back timing-based prompts for players who have turned them off.
Gives how long the game will wait between presses before treating them as separate rather than as a double tap, in seconds. Use it for abilities that have to fit inside that window.
Gives how quickly the view follows the action during a battle, as the player has set it.
Gives the multiplier the player has set for how fast dialog text appears.
Returns 1 when the player has asked the game to favour keyboard controls, otherwise 0. Use it to word prompts for keys rather than for the mouse.
Returns 1 when the player has asked the game to pause whenever the window loses focus, otherwise 0.
Gives how large the player has set the cursor. Use it for interface work that must size itself to match.
Gives how large the player has set the tooltips. Use it for interface work that must size itself to match.
Gives how wide the drawing surface is in game pixels, before the picture is scaled up to the window. Use it for laying out interface elements against the edges of the view.
Gives how tall the drawing surface is in game pixels, before the picture is scaled up to the window. Use it for laying out interface elements against the edges of the view.
Gives how wide the game window is after the picture has been scaled up, in real screen pixels. Pair it with the drawing-surface width to work out the current scaling.
Gives how tall the game window is after the picture has been scaled up, in real screen pixels. Pair it with the drawing-surface height to work out the current scaling.
Returns 1 when the game window is maximised, otherwise 0.
Gives how wide the player's monitor is, in real screen pixels. Use it where a layout must know what the display can actually hold.
Gives how tall the player's monitor is, in real screen pixels. Use it where a layout must know what the display can actually hold.
Gives the width the player has chosen for fullscreen play, in real screen pixels. It reports the setting whether or not the game is currently fullscreen.
Gives the height the player has chosen for fullscreen play, in real screen pixels. It reports the setting whether or not the game is currently fullscreen.
Always gives 0. It was meant to report damaged saved zones but the check has been emptied out, so nothing can make it report anything else.

Counts the caster's own pillburrows within a number of tiles of it, the range coming from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. It is a purpose-built reading for the creature that spawns from them rather than a general-purpose one.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the caster to search. Left out, the search covers the caster's own tile only.

uses.description: Counts the caster's own heart segments within a number of tiles of it, the range coming from the figure supplied in brackets after the name. It is a purpose-built reading for that particular creature rather than a general-purpose one.

arguments.name: radius
arguments.description: How many tiles out from the caster to search. Left out, the search covers the caster's own tile only.
